# page

[](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/edit/main/docs/examples/features/logging_configuration.md "Edit this page")

Source [https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/features/logging\_configuration.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/features/logging_configuration.md).

vLLM leverages Python's `logging.config.dictConfig` functionality to enable robust and flexible configuration of the various loggers used by vLLM.

vLLM offers two environment variables that can be used to accommodate a range of logging configurations that range from simple-and-inflexible to more-complex-and-more-flexible.

-   No vLLM logging (simple and inflexible)
    -   Set `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING=0` (leaving `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` unset)
-   vLLM's default logging configuration (simple and inflexible)
    -   Leave `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING` unset or set `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING=1`
-   Fine-grained custom logging configuration (more complex, more flexible)
    -   Leave `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING` unset or set `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING=1` and set `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH=<path-to-logging-config.json>`

## Logging Configuration Environment Variables[¶](#logging-configuration-environment-variables "Permanent link")

### `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING`[¶](#vllm_configure_logging "Permanent link")

`VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING` controls whether or not vLLM takes any action to configure the loggers used by vLLM. This functionality is enabled by default, but can be disabled by setting `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING=0` when running vLLM.

If `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING` is enabled and no value is given for `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH`, vLLM will use built-in default configuration to configure the root vLLM logger. By default, no other vLLM loggers are configured and, as such, all vLLM loggers defer to the root vLLM logger to make all logging decisions.

If `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING` is disabled and a value is given for `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH`, an error will occur while starting vLLM.

### `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH`[¶](#vllm_logging_config_path "Permanent link")

`VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` allows users to specify a path to a JSON file of alternative, custom logging configuration that will be used instead of vLLM's built-in default logging configuration. The logging configuration should be provided in JSON format following the schema specified by Python's [logging configuration dictionary schema](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.config.html#dictionary-schema-details).

If `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` is specified, but `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING` is disabled, an error will occur while starting vLLM.

## Examples[¶](#examples "Permanent link")

### Example 1: Customize vLLM root logger[¶](#example-1-customize-vllm-root-logger "Permanent link")

For this example, we will customize the vLLM root logger to use [`python-json-logger`](https://github.com/nhairs/python-json-logger) (which is part of the container image) to log to STDOUT of the console in JSON format with a log level of `INFO`.

To begin, first, create an appropriate JSON logging configuration file:

/path/to/logging\_config.json

`[](#__codelineno-0-1){   [](#__codelineno-0-2)  "formatters": {    [](#__codelineno-0-3)    "json": {      [](#__codelineno-0-4)      "class": "pythonjsonlogger.jsonlogger.JsonFormatter"    [](#__codelineno-0-5)    }  [](#__codelineno-0-6)  },  [](#__codelineno-0-7)  "handlers": {    [](#__codelineno-0-8)    "console": {      [](#__codelineno-0-9)      "class" : "logging.StreamHandler",      [](#__codelineno-0-10)      "formatter": "json",      [](#__codelineno-0-11)      "level": "INFO",      [](#__codelineno-0-12)      "stream": "ext://sys.stdout"    [](#__codelineno-0-13)    }  [](#__codelineno-0-14)  },  [](#__codelineno-0-15)  "loggers": {    [](#__codelineno-0-16)    "vllm": {      [](#__codelineno-0-17)      "handlers": ["console"],      [](#__codelineno-0-18)      "level": "INFO",      [](#__codelineno-0-19)      "propagate": false    [](#__codelineno-0-20)    }  [](#__codelineno-0-21)  },  [](#__codelineno-0-22)  "version": 1 [](#__codelineno-0-23)}`

Finally, run vLLM with the `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` environment variable set to the path of the custom logging configuration JSON file:

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/logging_config.json \     [](#__codelineno-1-2)    vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 --max-model-len 2048`

### Example 2: Silence a particular vLLM logger[¶](#example-2-silence-a-particular-vllm-logger "Permanent link")

To silence a particular vLLM logger, it is necessary to provide custom logging configuration for the target logger that configures the logger so that it won't propagate its log messages to the root vLLM logger.

When custom configuration is provided for any logger, it is also necessary to provide configuration for the root vLLM logger since any custom logger configuration overrides the built-in default logging configuration used by vLLM.

First, create an appropriate JSON logging configuration file that includes configuration for the root vLLM logger and for the logger you wish to silence:

/path/to/logging\_config.json

`[](#__codelineno-2-1){   [](#__codelineno-2-2)  "formatters": {    [](#__codelineno-2-3)    "vllm": {      [](#__codelineno-2-4)      "class": "vllm.logging_utils.NewLineFormatter",      [](#__codelineno-2-5)      "datefmt": "%m-%d %H:%M:%S",      [](#__codelineno-2-6)      "format": "%(levelname)s %(asctime)s %(filename)s:%(lineno)d] %(message)s"    [](#__codelineno-2-7)    }  [](#__codelineno-2-8)  },  [](#__codelineno-2-9)  "handlers": {    [](#__codelineno-2-10)    "vllm": {      [](#__codelineno-2-11)      "class" : "logging.StreamHandler",      [](#__codelineno-2-12)      "formatter": "vllm",      [](#__codelineno-2-13)      "level": "INFO",      [](#__codelineno-2-14)      "stream": "ext://sys.stdout"    [](#__codelineno-2-15)    }  [](#__codelineno-2-16)  },  [](#__codelineno-2-17)  "loggers": {    [](#__codelineno-2-18)    "vllm": {      [](#__codelineno-2-19)      "handlers": ["vllm"],      [](#__codelineno-2-20)      "level": "DEBUG",      [](#__codelineno-2-21)      "propagate": false    [](#__codelineno-2-22)    },    [](#__codelineno-2-23)    "vllm.example_noisy_logger": {      [](#__codelineno-2-24)      "propagate": false    [](#__codelineno-2-25)    }  [](#__codelineno-2-26)  },  [](#__codelineno-2-27)  "version": 1 [](#__codelineno-2-28)}`

Finally, run vLLM with the `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` environment variable set to the path of the custom logging configuration JSON file:

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/logging_config.json \     [](#__codelineno-3-2)    vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 --max-model-len 2048`

### Example 3: Disable vLLM default logging configuration[¶](#example-3-disable-vllm-default-logging-configuration "Permanent link")

To disable vLLM's default logging configuration and silence all vLLM loggers, simple set `VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING=0` when running vLLM. This will prevent vLLM for configuring the root vLLM logger, which in turn, silences all other vLLM loggers.

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING=0 \     [](#__codelineno-4-2)    vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 --max-model-len 2048`

### Example 4: Disable access logs for health check endpoints[¶](#example-4-disable-access-logs-for-health-check-endpoints "Permanent link")

In production environments, health check endpoints like `/health`, `/metrics`, and `/ping` are frequently called by load balancers and monitoring systems, generating a large volume of repetitive access logs. To reduce log noise while keeping logs for other endpoints, use the `--disable-access-log-for-endpoints` option.

**Disable access logs for health and metrics endpoints:**

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 --max-model-len 2048 \     [](#__codelineno-5-2)    --disable-access-log-for-endpoints /health,/metrics,/ping`

**Common endpoints to consider filtering:**

Endpoint

Description

Typical Caller

`/health`

Health check

Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes, load balancers

`/metrics`

Prometheus metrics

Prometheus scraper (every 15-60s)

`/ping`

SageMaker health check

SageMaker infrastructure

`/load`

Server load metrics

Custom monitoring

**Notes:**

-   This option only affects uvicorn access logs, not vLLM application logs
-   Specify multiple endpoints by separating them with commas (no spaces)
-   The filter uses exact path matching, query parameters are ignored (e.g., `/health?verbose=true` matches `/health`)
-   If you need to completely disable all access logs, use `--disable-uvicorn-access-log` instead

## Additional resources[¶](#additional-resources "Permanent link")

-   [`logging.config` Dictionary Schema Details](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.config.html#dictionary-schema-details)

# page

[](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/edit/main/docs/examples/features/logits_processor.md "Edit this page")

Source [https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples/features/logits\_processor](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples/features/logits_processor).

This directory contains examples demonstrating how to use custom logits processors with vLLM's offline inference API. Logits processors allow you to modify the model's output distribution before sampling, enabling controlled generation behaviors like token masking, constrained decoding, and custom sampling strategies.

## Scripts[¶](#scripts "Permanent link")

### `custom.py` — Engine-level logits processor[¶](#custompy-engine-level-logits-processor "Permanent link")

Demonstrates how to instantiate vLLM with a custom logits processor class that operates at the batch level. The example uses a `DummyLogitsProcessor` that masks out all tokens except a specified `target_token` when passed via `SamplingParams.extra_args`.

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)python examples/features/logits_processor/custom.py`

### `custom_req.py` — Request-level logits processor wrapper[¶](#custom_reqpy-request-level-logits-processor-wrapper "Permanent link")

Shows how to wrap a request-level logits processor (which operates on individual requests) to be compatible with vLLM's batch-level logits processing interface.

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)python examples/features/logits_processor/custom_req.py`

### `custom_req_init.py` — Request-level processor with engine config[¶](#custom_req_initpy-request-level-processor-with-engine-config "Permanent link")

A special case of wrapping a request-level logits processor where the processor needs access to engine configuration or model metadata during initialization (e.g., vocabulary size, tokenizer info).

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)python examples/features/logits_processor/custom_req_init.py`

## Key Concepts[¶](#key-concepts "Permanent link")

-   **Batch-level vs. request-level**: vLLM processes logits at the batch level for efficiency. If you have a per-request processor, you need to wrap it using the patterns shown in `custom_req.py` and `custom_req_init.py`.
-   **`SamplingParams.extra_args`**: Use this to pass custom keyword arguments to your logits processor on a per-request basis (e.g., `target_token`).
-   **`DummyLogitsProcessor`**: A reference implementation available in `vllm/test_utils.py` that can be used as a starting point for custom processors.

## Further Reading[¶](#further-reading "Permanent link")

-   [vLLM Sampling Parameters](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/inference_params.html#sampling-parameters)
-   [vLLM LLM API](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/offline_inference/llm.html)

## Example materials[¶](#example-materials "Permanent link")

# page

[](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/edit/main/docs/examples/features/openai_batch.md "Edit this page")

Source [https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples/features/openai\_batch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples/features/openai_batch).

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)This is a guide to performing batch inference using the OpenAI batch file format, **not** the complete Batch (REST) API.`

## File Format[¶](#file-format "Permanent link")

The OpenAI batch file format consists of a series of json objects on new lines.

[See here for an example file.](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl)

Each line represents a separate request. See the [OpenAI package reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/batch/requestInput) for more details.

``[](#__codelineno-1-1)We currently support `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, and `/v1/score` endpoints (completions coming soon).``

## Pre-requisites[¶](#pre-requisites "Permanent link")

-   The examples in this document use `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct`.
    -   Create a [user access token](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/security-tokens)
    -   Install the token on your machine (Run `hf auth login`).
    -   Get access to the gated model by [visiting the model card](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct) and agreeing to the terms and conditions.

## Example 1: Running with a local file[¶](#example-1-running-with-a-local-file "Permanent link")

### Step 1: Create your batch file[¶](#step-1-create-your-batch-file "Permanent link")

To follow along with this example, you can download the example batch, or create your own batch file in your working directory.

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/examples/features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl`

Once you've created your batch file it should look like this

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)cat features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl [](#__codelineno-3-2){"custom_id": "request-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions", "body": {"model": "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct", "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},{"role": "user", "content": "Hello world!"}],"max_completion_tokens": 1000}} [](#__codelineno-3-3){"custom_id": "request-2", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions", "body": {"model": "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct", "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are an unhelpful assistant."},{"role": "user", "content": "Hello world!"}],"max_completion_tokens": 1000}}`

### Step 2: Run the batch[¶](#step-2-run-the-batch "Permanent link")

The batch running tool is designed to be used from the command line.

You can run the batch with the following command, which will write its results to a file called `results.jsonl`

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.run_batch \     [](#__codelineno-4-2)    -i features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl \    [](#__codelineno-4-3)    -o results.jsonl \    [](#__codelineno-4-4)    --model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct`

or use command-line:

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)vllm run-batch \     [](#__codelineno-5-2)    -i features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl \    [](#__codelineno-5-3)    -o results.jsonl \    [](#__codelineno-5-4)    --model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct`

### Step 3: Check your results[¶](#step-3-check-your-results "Permanent link")

You should now have your results at `results.jsonl`. You can check your results by running `cat results.jsonl`

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)cat results.jsonl [](#__codelineno-6-2){"id":"vllm-383d1c59835645aeb2e07d004d62a826","custom_id":"request-1","response":{"id":"cmpl-61c020e54b964d5a98fa7527bfcdd378","object":"chat.completion","created":1715633336,"model":"meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Hello! It's great to meet you! I'm here to help with any questions or tasks you may have. What's on your mind today?"},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop","stop_reason":null}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":25,"total_tokens":56,"completion_tokens":31}},"error":null} [](#__codelineno-6-3){"id":"vllm-42e3d09b14b04568afa3f1797751a267","custom_id":"request-2","response":{"id":"cmpl-f44d049f6b3a42d4b2d7850bb1e31bcc","object":"chat.completion","created":1715633336,"model":"meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"*silence*"},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop","stop_reason":null}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":27,"total_tokens":32,"completion_tokens":5}},"error":null}`

## Example 2: Using remote files[¶](#example-2-using-remote-files "Permanent link")

The batch runner supports remote input and output urls that are accessible via http/https.

For example, to run against our example input file located at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/examples/features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl`, you can run

`[](#__codelineno-7-1)python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.run_batch \     [](#__codelineno-7-2)    -i https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/examples/features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl \    [](#__codelineno-7-3)    -o results.jsonl \    [](#__codelineno-7-4)    --model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct`

or use command-line:

`[](#__codelineno-8-1)vllm run-batch \     [](#__codelineno-8-2)    -i https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/examples/features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl \    [](#__codelineno-8-3)    -o results.jsonl \    [](#__codelineno-8-4)    --model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct`

## Example 3: Integrating with AWS S3[¶](#example-3-integrating-with-aws-s3 "Permanent link")

To integrate with cloud blob storage, we recommend using presigned urls.

\[Learn more about S3 presigned urls here\]

### Additional prerequisites[¶](#additional-prerequisites "Permanent link")

-   [Create an S3 bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/creating-bucket.html).
-   The `awscli` package (Run `pip install awscli`) to configure your credentials and interactively use s3.
    -   [Configure your credentials](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-quickstart.html).
-   The `boto3` python package (Run `pip install boto3`) to generate presigned urls.

### Step 1: Upload your input script[¶](#step-1-upload-your-input-script "Permanent link")

To follow along with this example, you can download the example batch, or create your own batch file in your working directory.

`[](#__codelineno-9-1)wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/examples/features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl`

Once you've created your batch file it should look like this

`[](#__codelineno-10-1)cat features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl [](#__codelineno-10-2){"custom_id": "request-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions", "body": {"model": "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct", "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},{"role": "user", "content": "Hello world!"}],"max_completion_tokens": 1000}} [](#__codelineno-10-3){"custom_id": "request-2", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions", "body": {"model": "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct", "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are an unhelpful assistant."},{"role": "user", "content": "Hello world!"}],"max_completion_tokens": 1000}}`

Now upload your batch file to your S3 bucket.

`[](#__codelineno-11-1)aws s3 cp features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl s3://MY_BUCKET/MY_INPUT_FILE.jsonl`

### Step 2: Generate your presigned urls[¶](#step-2-generate-your-presigned-urls "Permanent link")

Presigned urls can only be generated via the SDK. You can run the following python script to generate your presigned urls. Be sure to replace the `MY_BUCKET`, `MY_INPUT_FILE.jsonl`, and `MY_OUTPUT_FILE.jsonl` placeholders with your bucket and file names.

(The script is adapted from [https://github.com/awsdocs/aws-doc-sdk-examples/blob/main/python/example\_code/s3/s3\_basics/presigned\_url.py](https://github.com/awsdocs/aws-doc-sdk-examples/blob/main/python/example_code/s3/s3_basics/presigned_url.py))

`[](#__codelineno-12-1)import boto3 [](#__codelineno-12-2)from botocore.exceptions import ClientError [](#__codelineno-12-3)[](#__codelineno-12-4)def generate_presigned_url(s3_client, client_method, method_parameters, expires_in):     [](#__codelineno-12-5)    """    [](#__codelineno-12-6)    Generate a presigned Amazon S3 URL that can be used to perform an action. [](#__codelineno-12-7)    [](#__codelineno-12-8)    :param s3_client: A Boto3 Amazon S3 client.    [](#__codelineno-12-9)    :param client_method: The name of the client method that the URL performs.    [](#__codelineno-12-10)    :param method_parameters: The parameters of the specified client method.    [](#__codelineno-12-11)    :param expires_in: The number of seconds the presigned URL is valid for.    [](#__codelineno-12-12)    :return: The presigned URL.    [](#__codelineno-12-13)    """    [](#__codelineno-12-14)    try:        [](#__codelineno-12-15)        url = s3_client.generate_presigned_url(            [](#__codelineno-12-16)            ClientMethod=client_method,            [](#__codelineno-12-17)            Params=method_parameters,            [](#__codelineno-12-18)            ExpiresIn=expires_in,        [](#__codelineno-12-19)        )    [](#__codelineno-12-20)    except ClientError:        [](#__codelineno-12-21)        raise    [](#__codelineno-12-22)    return url [](#__codelineno-12-23) [](#__codelineno-12-24)[](#__codelineno-12-25)s3_client = boto3.client("s3") [](#__codelineno-12-26)input_url = generate_presigned_url(     [](#__codelineno-12-27)    s3_client,    [](#__codelineno-12-28)    "get_object",    [](#__codelineno-12-29)    {"Bucket": "MY_BUCKET", "Key": "MY_INPUT_FILE.jsonl"},    [](#__codelineno-12-30)    expires_in=3600, [](#__codelineno-12-31)) [](#__codelineno-12-32)output_url = generate_presigned_url(     [](#__codelineno-12-33)    s3_client,    [](#__codelineno-12-34)    "put_object",    [](#__codelineno-12-35)    {"Bucket": "MY_BUCKET", "Key": "MY_OUTPUT_FILE.jsonl"},    [](#__codelineno-12-36)    expires_in=3600, [](#__codelineno-12-37)) [](#__codelineno-12-38)print(f"{input_url=}") [](#__codelineno-12-39)print(f"{output_url=}")`

This script should output

`[](#__codelineno-13-1)input_url='https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/MY_BUCKET/MY_INPUT_FILE.jsonl?AWSAccessKeyId=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRST&Signature=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz12345&Expires=1715800091' [](#__codelineno-13-2)output_url='https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/MY_BUCKET/MY_OUTPUT_FILE.jsonl?AWSAccessKeyId=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRST&Signature=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz12345&Expires=1715800091'`

### Step 3: Run the batch runner using your presigned urls[¶](#step-3-run-the-batch-runner-using-your-presigned-urls "Permanent link")

You can now run the batch runner, using the urls generated in the previous section.

`[](#__codelineno-14-1)python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.run_batch \     [](#__codelineno-14-2)    -i "https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/MY_BUCKET/MY_INPUT_FILE.jsonl?AWSAccessKeyId=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRST&Signature=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz12345&Expires=1715800091" \    [](#__codelineno-14-3)    -o "https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/MY_BUCKET/MY_OUTPUT_FILE.jsonl?AWSAccessKeyId=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRST&Signature=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz12345&Expires=1715800091" \    [](#__codelineno-14-4)    --model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct`

or use command-line:

`[](#__codelineno-15-1)vllm run-batch \     [](#__codelineno-15-2)    -i "https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/MY_BUCKET/MY_INPUT_FILE.jsonl?AWSAccessKeyId=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRST&Signature=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz12345&Expires=1715800091" \    [](#__codelineno-15-3)    -o "https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/MY_BUCKET/MY_OUTPUT_FILE.jsonl?AWSAccessKeyId=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRST&Signature=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz12345&Expires=1715800091" \    [](#__codelineno-15-4)    --model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct`

### Step 4: View your results[¶](#step-4-view-your-results "Permanent link")

Your results are now on S3. You can view them in your terminal by running

`[](#__codelineno-16-1)aws s3 cp s3://MY_BUCKET/MY_OUTPUT_FILE.jsonl -`

## Example 4: Using embeddings endpoint[¶](#example-4-using-embeddings-endpoint "Permanent link")

### Additional prerequisites[¶](#additional-prerequisites_1 "Permanent link")

-   Ensure you are using `vllm >= 0.5.5`.

### Step 1: Create your batch file[¶](#step-1-create-your-batch-file_1 "Permanent link")

Add embedding requests to your batch file. The following is an example:

`[](#__codelineno-17-1){"custom_id": "request-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "intfloat/e5-mistral-7b-instruct", "input": "You are a helpful assistant."}} [](#__codelineno-17-2){"custom_id": "request-2", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "intfloat/e5-mistral-7b-instruct", "input": "You are an unhelpful assistant."}}`

You can even mix chat completion and embedding requests in the batch file, as long as the model you are using supports both chat completion and embeddings (note that all requests must use the same model).

### Step 2: Run the batch[¶](#step-2-run-the-batch_1 "Permanent link")

You can run the batch using the same command as in earlier examples.

### Step 3: Check your results[¶](#step-3-check-your-results_1 "Permanent link")

You can check your results by running `cat results.jsonl`

`[](#__codelineno-18-1)cat results.jsonl [](#__codelineno-18-2){"id":"vllm-db0f71f7dec244e6bce530e0b4ef908b","custom_id":"request-1","response":{"status_code":200,"request_id":"vllm-batch-3580bf4d4ae54d52b67eee266a6eab20","body":{"id":"embd-33ac2efa7996430184461f2e38529746","object":"list","created":444647,"model":"intfloat/e5-mistral-7b-instruct","data":[{"index":0,"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.016204833984375,0.0092010498046875,0.0018358230590820312,-0.0028228759765625,0.001422882080078125,-0.0031147003173828125,...]}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":8,"total_tokens":8,"completion_tokens":0}}},"error":null} [](#__codelineno-18-3)...`

## Example 5: Using score endpoint[¶](#example-5-using-score-endpoint "Permanent link")

### Additional prerequisites[¶](#additional-prerequisites_2 "Permanent link")

-   Ensure you are using `vllm >= 0.7.0`.

### Step 1: Create your batch file[¶](#step-1-create-your-batch-file_2 "Permanent link")

Add score requests to your batch file. The following is an example:

`[](#__codelineno-19-1){"custom_id": "request-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/score", "body": {"model": "BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", "queries": "What is the capital of France?", "documents": ["The capital of Brazil is Brasilia.", "The capital of France is Paris."]}} [](#__codelineno-19-2){"custom_id": "request-2", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/score", "body": {"model": "BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", "queries": "What is the capital of France?", "documents": ["The capital of Brazil is Brasilia.", "The capital of France is Paris."]}}`

You can mix chat completion, embedding, and score requests in the batch file, as long as the model you are using supports them all (note that all requests must use the same model).

### Step 2: Run the batch[¶](#step-2-run-the-batch_2 "Permanent link")

You can run the batch using the same command as in earlier examples.

### Step 3: Check your results[¶](#step-3-check-your-results_2 "Permanent link")

You can check your results by running `cat results.jsonl`

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-1-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-1-3)"""Test for pause/resume with keep mode. [](#__codelineno-1-58)        nonlocal pause_time, resume_time, pause_token_idx [](#__codelineno-1-59)        [](#__codelineno-1-60)        # Wait for some tokens to be generated        [](#__codelineno-1-61)        while len(token_times) < 5:            [](#__codelineno-1-62)            await asyncio.sleep(0.01) [](#__codelineno-1-63)        [](#__codelineno-1-64)        print(f"\nPausing engine (keep mode) at token {len(token_times)}")        [](#__codelineno-1-65)        pause_time = time.monotonic()        [](#__codelineno-1-66)        await engine.pause_generation(mode="keep")        [](#__codelineno-1-67)        pause_token_idx = len(token_times)        [](#__codelineno-1-68)        print(f"Paused! Sleeping for {PAUSE_DURATION}s...") [](#__codelineno-1-69)        [](#__codelineno-1-70)        # Sleep while paused - no tokens should be generated during this time        [](#__codelineno-1-71)        await asyncio.sleep(PAUSE_DURATION) [](#__codelineno-1-72)        [](#__codelineno-1-73)        print("Resuming engine...") ## Prompt Embed Inference With OpenAI Client[¶](#prompt-embed-inference-with-openai-client "Permanent link")

``[](#__codelineno-0-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-0-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-0-3)"""vLLM OpenAI-Compatible Client with Prompt Embeddings. [](#__codelineno-0-4)[](#__codelineno-0-5)This script demonstrates how to: [](#__codelineno-0-6)1. Generate prompt embeddings using Hugging Face Transformers. [](#__codelineno-0-7)2. Encode them in base64 format. [](#__codelineno-0-8)3. Send them to a vLLM server for inference via both:     [](#__codelineno-0-9)    - OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API    [](#__codelineno-0-10)    - OpenAI-compatible Completions API [](#__codelineno-0-11)[](#__codelineno-0-12)Important distinction between the two APIs: [](#__codelineno-0-13)[](#__codelineno-0-14)- Chat Completions API: `prompt_embeds` content parts should encode ONLY   [](#__codelineno-0-15)  the user-provided content, not a templated conversation. The server  [](#__codelineno-0-16)  renders the surrounding chat template around the embedded content at  [](#__codelineno-0-17)  request time, the same way it would for a plain text `content` string.  [](#__codelineno-0-18)  Embedding a full templated conversation here would double-apply the  [](#__codelineno-0-19)  template and likely produce undesirable results. [](#__codelineno-0-20)[](#__codelineno-0-21)- Completions API: the server does NOT apply a chat template to   [](#__codelineno-0-22)  `prompt_embeds`. The caller is responsible for producing embeddings for  [](#__codelineno-0-23)  the full, already-templated prompt (i.e. apply the chat template first,  [](#__codelineno-0-24)  then embed the resulting token IDs). Anything the model would normally  [](#__codelineno-0-25)  need (system prompt, role markers, generation prompt, etc.) must already  [](#__codelineno-0-26)  be baked into the embedded tokens. [](#__codelineno-0-27)[](#__codelineno-0-28)Run the vLLM server first: [](#__codelineno-0-29)vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct \   [](#__codelineno-0-30)  --runner generate \  [](#__codelineno-0-31)  --max-model-len 4096 \  [](#__codelineno-0-32)  --enable-prompt-embeds [](#__codelineno-0-33)[](#__codelineno-0-34)Run the client: [](#__codelineno-0-35)python examples/features/prompt_embed/prompt_embed_inference_with_openai_client.py [](#__codelineno-0-36)[](#__codelineno-0-37)Model: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct [](#__codelineno-0-38)Note: This model is gated on Hugging Face Hub. # page

[](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/edit/main/docs/examples/features/structured_outputs.md "Edit this page")

Source [https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples/features/structured\_outputs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples/features/structured_outputs).

This script demonstrates various structured output capabilities of vLLM's OpenAI-compatible server. It can run individual constraint type or all of them. It supports both streaming responses and concurrent non-streaming requests.

To use this example, you must start an vLLM server with any model of your choice.

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct`

To serve a reasoning model, you can use the following command:

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B \     [](#__codelineno-1-2)    --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1`

If you want to run this script standalone with `uv`, you can use the following:

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)uvx --from git+https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm#subdirectory=examples/features/structured_outputs \     [](#__codelineno-2-2)    structured-outputs`

See [feature docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/structured_outputs.html) for more information.

Tip

If vLLM is running remotely, then set `OPENAI_BASE_URL=<remote_url>` before running the script.

## Usage[¶](#usage "Permanent link")

Run all constraints, non-streaming:

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)uv run structured_outputs_offline.py`

Run all constraints, streaming:

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)uv run structured_outputs_offline.py --stream`

Run certain constraints, for example `structural_tag` and `regex`, streaming:

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)uv run structured_outputs_offline.py \     [](#__codelineno-5-2)    --constraint structural_tag regex \    [](#__codelineno-5-3)    --stream`

Run all constraints, with reasoning models and streaming:

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)uv run structured_outputs_offline.py --reasoning --stream`

## Example materials[¶](#example-materials "Permanent link")

``[](#__codelineno-0-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-0-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-0-3)[](#__codelineno-0-4)import json [](#__codelineno-0-5)import logging [](#__codelineno-0-6)import os [](#__codelineno-0-7)import uuid [](#__codelineno-0-8)[](#__codelineno-0-9)from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams [](#__codelineno-0-10)from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs [](#__codelineno-0-11)from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest [](#__codelineno-0-12)from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.tensorizer import (     [](#__codelineno-0-13)    TensorizerArgs,    [](#__codelineno-0-14)    TensorizerConfig,    [](#__codelineno-0-15)    tensorize_lora_adapter,    [](#__codelineno-0-16)    tensorize_vllm_model,    [](#__codelineno-0-17)    tensorizer_kwargs_arg, [](#__codelineno-0-18)) [](#__codelineno-0-19)from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser [](#__codelineno-0-20)[](#__codelineno-0-21)logger = logging.getLogger() [](#__codelineno-0-22) [](#__codelineno-0-23)[](#__codelineno-0-24)""" [](#__codelineno-0-25)tensorize_vllm_model.py is a script that can be used to serialize and  [](#__codelineno-0-26)deserialize vLLM models. These models can be loaded using tensorizer  [](#__codelineno-0-27)to the GPU extremely quickly over an HTTP/HTTPS endpoint, an S3 endpoint, [](#__codelineno-0-28)or locally. Tensor encryption and decryption is also supported, although  [](#__codelineno-0-29)libsodium must be installed to use it. Install vllm with tensorizer support  [](#__codelineno-0-30)using `pip install vllm[tensorizer]`. To learn more about tensorizer, visit [](#__codelineno-0-31)https://github.com/coreweave/tensorizer [](#__codelineno-0-32)[](#__codelineno-0-33)To serialize a model, install vLLM from source, then run something  [](#__codelineno-0-34)like this from the root level of this repository: [](#__codelineno-0-35)[](#__codelineno-0-36)python examples/features/tensorize_vllm_model.py \    [](#__codelineno-0-37)   --model facebook/opt-125m \   [](#__codelineno-0-38)   serialize \   [](#__codelineno-0-39)   --serialized-directory s3://my-bucket \   [](#__codelineno-0-40)   --suffix v1 [](#__codelineno-0-41)[](#__codelineno-0-42)Which downloads the model from HuggingFace, loads it into vLLM, serializes it, [](#__codelineno-0-43)and saves it to your S3 bucket. A local directory can also be used. This [](#__codelineno-0-44)assumes your S3 credentials are specified as environment variables [](#__codelineno-0-45)in the form of `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and  [](#__codelineno-0-46)`S3_ENDPOINT_URL`. To provide S3 credentials directly, you can provide  [](#__codelineno-0-47)`--s3-access-key-id` and `--s3-secret-access-key`, as well as `--s3-endpoint`  [](#__codelineno-0-48)as CLI args to this script. [](#__codelineno-0-49)[](#__codelineno-0-50)You can also encrypt the model weights with a randomly-generated key by  [](#__codelineno-0-51)providing a `--keyfile` argument. [](#__codelineno-0-52)[](#__codelineno-0-53)To deserialize a model, you can run something like this from the root  [](#__codelineno-0-54)level of this repository: [](#__codelineno-0-55)[](#__codelineno-0-56)python examples/features/tensorize_vllm_model.py \    [](#__codelineno-0-57)   --model EleutherAI/gpt-j-6B \   [](#__codelineno-0-58)   --dtype float16 \   [](#__codelineno-0-59)   deserialize \   [](#__codelineno-0-60)   --path-to-tensors s3://my-bucket/vllm/EleutherAI/gpt-j-6B/v1/model.tensors [](#__codelineno-0-61)[](#__codelineno-0-62)Which downloads the model tensors from your S3 bucket and deserializes them. [](#__codelineno-0-63)[](#__codelineno-0-64)You can also provide a `--keyfile` argument to decrypt the model weights if  [](#__codelineno-0-65)they were serialized with encryption. [](#__codelineno-0-66)[](#__codelineno-0-67)To support distributed tensor-parallel models, each model shard will be [](#__codelineno-0-68)serialized to a separate file. The tensorizer_uri is then specified as a string [](#__codelineno-0-69)template with a format specifier such as '%03d' that will be rendered with the [](#__codelineno-0-70)shard's rank. Sharded models serialized with this script will be named as [](#__codelineno-0-71)model-rank-%03d.tensors [](#__codelineno-0-72)[](#__codelineno-0-73)For more information on the available arguments for serializing, run  [](#__codelineno-0-74)`python -m examples.features.tensorize_vllm_model serialize --help`. [](#__codelineno-0-75)[](#__codelineno-0-76)Or for deserializing: [](#__codelineno-0-77)[](#__codelineno-0-78)`python examples/features/tensorize_vllm_model.py deserialize --help`. [](#__codelineno-0-79)[](#__codelineno-0-80)Once a model is serialized, tensorizer can be invoked with the `LLM` class  [](#__codelineno-0-81)directly to load models: [](#__codelineno-0-82)[](#__codelineno-0-83)```python [](#__codelineno-0-84)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-0-85)llm = LLM(     [](#__codelineno-0-86)    "s3://my-bucket/vllm/facebook/opt-125m/v1",    [](#__codelineno-0-87)    load_format="tensorizer", [](#__codelineno-0-88)) [](#__codelineno-0-89)``` [](#__codelineno-0-90) [](#__codelineno-0-91)[](#__codelineno-0-92)A serialized model can be used during model loading for the vLLM OpenAI [](#__codelineno-0-93)inference server: [](#__codelineno-0-94)[](#__codelineno-0-95)``` [](#__codelineno-0-96)vllm serve s3://my-bucket/vllm/facebook/opt-125m/v1 \     [](#__codelineno-0-97)    --load-format tensorizer [](#__codelineno-0-98)``` [](#__codelineno-0-99)[](#__codelineno-0-100)In order to see all of the available arguments usable to configure  [](#__codelineno-0-101)loading with tensorizer that are given to `TensorizerConfig`, run: [](#__codelineno-0-102)[](#__codelineno-0-103)`python examples/features/tensorize_vllm_model.py deserialize --help` [](#__codelineno-0-104)[](#__codelineno-0-105)under the `tensorizer options` section. These can also be used for [](#__codelineno-0-106)deserialization in this example script, although `--tensorizer-uri` and [](#__codelineno-0-107)`--path-to-tensors` are functionally the same in this case. [](#__codelineno-0-108)[](#__codelineno-0-109)Tensorizer can also be used to save and load LoRA adapters. A LoRA adapter [](#__codelineno-0-110)can be serialized directly with the path to the LoRA adapter on HF Hub and [](#__codelineno-0-111)a TensorizerConfig object. ` [](#__codelineno-4-1)# Qwen2.5-Omni Offline Inference Examples [](#__codelineno-4-2)[](#__codelineno-4-3)This folder provides several example scripts on how to inference Qwen2.5-Omni offline. [](#__codelineno-4-4)[](#__codelineno-4-5)## Thinker Only [](#__codelineno-4-6)[](#__codelineno-4-7)```bash [](#__codelineno-4-8)# Audio + image + video [](#__codelineno-4-9)python examples/generate/multimodal/qwen2_5_omni/only_thinker.py \     [](#__codelineno-4-10)    -q mixed_modalities [](#__codelineno-4-11)[](#__codelineno-4-12)# Read vision and audio inputs from a single video file [](#__codelineno-4-13)python examples/generate/multimodal/qwen2_5_omni/only_thinker.py \     [](#__codelineno-4-14)    -q use_audio_in_video [](#__codelineno-4-15)[](#__codelineno-4-16)# Multiple audios [](#__codelineno-4-17)python examples/generate/multimodal/qwen2_5_omni/only_thinker.py \     [](#__codelineno-4-18)    -q multi_audios [](#__codelineno-4-19)``` [](#__codelineno-4-20)[](#__codelineno-4-21)This script will run the thinker part of Qwen2.5-Omni, and generate text response. [](#__codelineno-4-22)[](#__codelineno-4-23)You can also test Qwen2.5-Omni on a single modality: [](#__codelineno-4-24)[](#__codelineno-4-25)```bash [](#__codelineno-4-26)# Process audio inputs [](#__codelineno-4-27)python examples/generate/multimodal/audio_language_offline.py \     [](#__codelineno-4-28)    --model-type qwen2_5_omni [](#__codelineno-4-29)[](#__codelineno-4-30)# Process image inputs [](#__codelineno-4-31)python examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py \     [](#__codelineno-4-32)    --modality image \    [](#__codelineno-4-33)    --model-type qwen2_5_omni [](#__codelineno-4-34)[](#__codelineno-4-35)# Process video inputs [](#__codelineno-4-36)python examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py \     [](#__codelineno-4-37)    --modality video \    [](#__codelineno-4-38)    --model-type qwen2_5_omni [](#__codelineno-4-39)``` `

## Offline[¶](#offline "Permanent link")

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-0-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-0-3)[](#__codelineno-0-4)from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams [](#__codelineno-0-5)from vllm.v1.metrics.reader import Counter, Gauge, Histogram, Vector [](#__codelineno-0-6)[](#__codelineno-0-7)# Sample prompts. [](#__codelineno-0-8)prompts = [     [](#__codelineno-0-9)    "Hello, my name is",    [](#__codelineno-0-10)    "The president of the United States is",    [](#__codelineno-0-11)    "The capital of France is",    [](#__codelineno-0-12)    "The future of AI is", [](#__codelineno-0-13)] [](#__codelineno-0-14)# Create a sampling params object. [](#__codelineno-0-15)sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95) [](#__codelineno-0-16) [](#__codelineno-0-17)[](#__codelineno-0-18)def main():     [](#__codelineno-0-19)    # Create an LLM.    [](#__codelineno-0-20)    llm = LLM(model="facebook/opt-125m", disable_log_stats=False) [](#__codelineno-0-21)    [](#__codelineno-0-22)    # Generate texts from the prompts.    [](#__codelineno-0-23)    outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params) [](#__codelineno-0-24)    [](#__codelineno-0-25)    # Print the outputs.    [](#__codelineno-0-26)    print("-" * 50)    [](#__codelineno-0-27)    for output in outputs:        [](#__codelineno-0-28)        prompt = output.prompt        [](#__codelineno-0-29)        generated_text = output.outputs[0].text        [](#__codelineno-0-30)        print(f"Prompt: {prompt!r}\nGenerated text: {generated_text!r}")        [](#__codelineno-0-31)        print("-" * 50) [](#__codelineno-0-32)    [](#__codelineno-0-33)    # Dump all metrics    [](#__codelineno-0-34)    for metric in llm.get_metrics():        [](#__codelineno-0-35)        if isinstance(metric, Gauge):            [](#__codelineno-0-36)            print(f"{metric.name} (gauge) = {metric.value}")        [](#__codelineno-0-37)        elif isinstance(metric, Counter):            [](#__codelineno-0-38)            print(f"{metric.name} (counter) = {metric.value}")        [](#__codelineno-0-39)        elif isinstance(metric, Vector):            [](#__codelineno-0-40)            print(f"{metric.name} (vector) = {metric.values}")        [](#__codelineno-0-41)        elif isinstance(metric, Histogram):            [](#__codelineno-0-42)            print(f"{metric.name} (histogram)")            [](#__codelineno-0-43)            print(f"    sum = {metric.sum}")            [](#__codelineno-0-44)            print(f"    count = {metric.count}")            [](#__codelineno-0-45)            for bucket_le, value in metric.buckets.items():                [](#__codelineno-0-46)                print(f"    {bucket_le} = {value}") [](#__codelineno-0-47) [](#__codelineno-0-48)[](#__codelineno-0-49)if __name__ == "__main__":     [](#__codelineno-0-50)    main()`

# page

[](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/edit/main/docs/examples/observability/opentelemetry.md "Edit this page")

Source [https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples/observability/opentelemetry](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples/observability/opentelemetry).

> **Note:** The core OpenTelemetry packages (`opentelemetry-sdk`, `opentelemetry-api`, `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp`, `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai`) are bundled with vLLM. Manual installation is not required.

1.  Start Jaeger in a docker container:
    
    `[](#__codelineno-0-1)# From: https://www.jaegertracing.io/docs/1.57/getting-started/ [](#__codelineno-0-2)docker run --rm --name jaeger \     [](#__codelineno-0-3)    -e COLLECTOR_ZIPKIN_HOST_PORT=:9411 \    [](#__codelineno-0-4)    -p 6831:6831/udp \    [](#__codelineno-0-5)    -p 6832:6832/udp \    [](#__codelineno-0-6)    -p 5778:5778 \    [](#__codelineno-0-7)    -p 16686:16686 \    [](#__codelineno-0-8)    -p 4317:4317 \    [](#__codelineno-0-9)    -p 4318:4318 \    [](#__codelineno-0-10)    -p 14250:14250 \    [](#__codelineno-0-11)    -p 14268:14268 \    [](#__codelineno-0-12)    -p 14269:14269 \    [](#__codelineno-0-13)    -p 9411:9411 \    [](#__codelineno-0-14)    jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.57`
    
2.  In a new shell, export Jaeger IP:
    
    `[](#__codelineno-1-1)export JAEGER_IP=$(docker inspect   --format '{{ .NetworkSettings.IPAddress }}' jaeger) [](#__codelineno-1-2)export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=grpc://$JAEGER_IP:4317`
    
    Then set vLLM's service name for OpenTelemetry, enable insecure connections to Jaeger and run vLLM:
    
    `[](#__codelineno-2-1)export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="vllm-server" [](#__codelineno-2-2)export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_INSECURE=true [](#__codelineno-2-3)vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --otlp-traces-endpoint="$OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT"`
    
3.  In a new shell, send requests with trace context from a dummy client
    
    `[](#__codelineno-3-1)export JAEGER_IP=$(docker inspect --format '{{ .NetworkSettings.IPAddress }}' jaeger) [](#__codelineno-3-2)export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=grpc://$JAEGER_IP:4317 [](#__codelineno-3-3)export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_INSECURE=true [](#__codelineno-3-4)export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="client-service" [](#__codelineno-3-5)python dummy_client.py`
    
4.  Open Jaeger webui: [http://localhost:16686/](http://localhost:16686/)
    
    In the search pane, select `vllm-server` service and hit `Find Traces`. You should get a list of traces, one for each request. [![Traces](https://i.imgur.com/GYHhFjo.png)](https://i.imgur.com/GYHhFjo.png)
    
5.  Clicking on a trace will show its spans and their tags. In this demo, each trace has 2 spans. One from the dummy client containing the prompt text and one from vLLM containing metadata about the request. [![Spans details](https://i.imgur.com/OPf6CBL.png)](https://i.imgur.com/OPf6CBL.png)
    

## Exporter Protocol[¶](#exporter-protocol "Permanent link")

OpenTelemetry supports either `grpc` or `http/protobuf` as the transport protocol for trace data in the exporter. By default, `grpc` is used. To set `http/protobuf` as the protocol, configure the `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL` environment variable as follows:

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf [](#__codelineno-4-2)export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=http://$JAEGER_IP:4318/v1/traces [](#__codelineno-4-3)vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --otlp-traces-endpoint="$OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT"`

## Instrumentation of FastAPI[¶](#instrumentation-of-fastapi "Permanent link")

OpenTelemetry allows automatic instrumentation of FastAPI.

1.  Install the instrumentation library
    
    `[](#__codelineno-5-1)pip install opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi`
    
2.  Run vLLM with `opentelemetry-instrument`
    
    `[](#__codelineno-6-1)opentelemetry-instrument vllm serve facebook/opt-125m`
    
3.  Send a request to vLLM and find its trace in Jaeger. It should contain spans from FastAPI.
    

[![FastAPI Spans](https://i.imgur.com/hywvoOJ.png)](https://i.imgur.com/hywvoOJ.png)

## Example materials[¶](#example-materials "Permanent link")

dummy\_client.py

`[](#__codelineno-7-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-7-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-7-3)[](#__codelineno-7-4)import requests [](#__codelineno-7-5)from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter [](#__codelineno-7-6)from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider [](#__codelineno-7-7)from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor, ConsoleSpanExporter [](#__codelineno-7-8)from opentelemetry.trace import SpanKind, set_tracer_provider [](#__codelineno-7-9)from opentelemetry.trace.propagation.tracecontext import TraceContextTextMapPropagator [](#__codelineno-7-10)[](#__codelineno-7-11)trace_provider = TracerProvider() [](#__codelineno-7-12)set_tracer_provider(trace_provider) [](#__codelineno-7-13)[](#__codelineno-7-14)trace_provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter())) [](#__codelineno-7-15)trace_provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(ConsoleSpanExporter())) [](#__codelineno-7-16)[](#__codelineno-7-17)tracer = trace_provider.get_tracer("dummy-client") [](#__codelineno-7-18)[](#__codelineno-7-19)url = "http://localhost:8000/v1/completions" [](#__codelineno-7-20)with tracer.start_as_current_span("client-span", kind=SpanKind.CLIENT) as span:     [](#__codelineno-7-21)    prompt = "San Francisco is a"    [](#__codelineno-7-22)    span.set_attribute("prompt", prompt)    [](#__codelineno-7-23)    headers = {}    [](#__codelineno-7-24)    TraceContextTextMapPropagator().inject(headers)    [](#__codelineno-7-25)    payload = {        [](#__codelineno-7-26)        "model": "facebook/opt-125m",        [](#__codelineno-7-27)        "prompt": prompt,        [](#__codelineno-7-28)        "max_tokens": 10,        [](#__codelineno-7-29)        "n": 3,        [](#__codelineno-7-30)        "use_beam_search": "true",        [](#__codelineno-7-31)        "temperature": 0.0,        [](#__codelineno-7-32)        # "stream": True,    [](#__codelineno-7-33)    }    [](#__codelineno-7-34)    response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)`

## OpenAI Embedding Long Text - Readme[¶](#openai-embedding-long-text-readme "Permanent link")

``[](#__codelineno-5-1)# Long Text Embedding with Chunked Processing [](#__codelineno-5-2)[](#__codelineno-5-3)This directory contains examples for using vLLM's **chunked processing** feature to handle long text embedding that exceeds the model's maximum context length. [](#__codelineno-5-4)[](#__codelineno-5-5)## 🚀 Quick Start [](#__codelineno-5-6)[](#__codelineno-5-7)### Start the Server [](#__codelineno-5-8)[](#__codelineno-5-9)Use the provided script to start a vLLM server with chunked processing enabled: [](#__codelineno-5-10)[](#__codelineno-5-11)```bash [](#__codelineno-5-12)# Basic usage (supports very long texts up to ~3M tokens) [](#__codelineno-5-13)./service.sh [](#__codelineno-5-14)[](#__codelineno-5-15)# Custom configuration with different models [](#__codelineno-5-16)MODEL_NAME="jinaai/jina-embeddings-v3" \ [](#__codelineno-5-17)MAX_EMBED_LEN=1048576 \ [](#__codelineno-5-18)./service.sh [](#__codelineno-5-19)[](#__codelineno-5-20)# For extremely long documents [](#__codelineno-5-21)MODEL_NAME="intfloat/multilingual-e5-large" \ [](#__codelineno-5-22)MAX_EMBED_LEN=3072000 \ [](#__codelineno-5-23)./service.sh [](#__codelineno-5-24)``` [](#__codelineno-5-25)[](#__codelineno-5-26)### Test Long Text Embedding [](#__codelineno-5-27)[](#__codelineno-5-28)Run the comprehensive test client: [](#__codelineno-5-29)[](#__codelineno-5-30)```bash [](#__codelineno-5-31)python client.py [](#__codelineno-5-32)``` [](#__codelineno-5-33)[](#__codelineno-5-34)## 📁 Files [](#__codelineno-5-35)[](#__codelineno-5-36)| File | Description | [](#__codelineno-5-37)| ---- | ----------- | [](#__codelineno-5-38)| `service.sh` | Server startup script with chunked processing enabled | [](#__codelineno-5-39)| `client.py` | Comprehensive test client for long text embedding | [](#__codelineno-5-40)[](#__codelineno-5-41)## ⚙️ Configuration [](#__codelineno-5-42)[](#__codelineno-5-43)### Server Configuration [](#__codelineno-5-44)[](#__codelineno-5-45)The key parameters for chunked processing are in the `--pooler-config`: [](#__codelineno-5-46)[](#__codelineno-5-47)```json [](#__codelineno-5-48){   [](#__codelineno-5-49)  "pooling_type": "auto",  [](#__codelineno-5-50)  "use_activation": true,  [](#__codelineno-5-51)  "enable_chunked_processing": true,  [](#__codelineno-5-52)  "max_embed_len": 3072000 [](#__codelineno-5-53)} [](#__codelineno-5-54)``` [](#__codelineno-5-55)[](#__codelineno-5-56)!!! note     [](#__codelineno-5-57)    `pooling_type` sets the model's own pooling strategy for processing within each chunk. The cross-chunk aggregation automatically uses MEAN strategy when input exceeds the model's native maximum length. [](#__codelineno-5-58)[](#__codelineno-5-59)#### Chunked Processing Behavior [](#__codelineno-5-60)[](#__codelineno-5-61)Chunked processing uses **MEAN aggregation** for cross-chunk combination when input exceeds the model's native maximum length: [](#__codelineno-5-62)[](#__codelineno-5-63)| Component | Behavior | Description | [](#__codelineno-5-64)| --------- | -------- | ----------- | [](#__codelineno-5-65)| **Within chunks** | Model's native pooling | Uses the model's configured pooling strategy | [](#__codelineno-5-66)| **Cross-chunk aggregation** | Always MEAN | Weighted averaging based on chunk token counts | [](#__codelineno-5-67)| **Performance** | Optimal | All chunks processed for complete semantic coverage | [](#__codelineno-5-68)[](#__codelineno-5-69)### Environment Variables [](#__codelineno-5-70)[](#__codelineno-5-71)| Variable | Default | Description | [](#__codelineno-5-72)| -------- | ------- | ----------- | [](#__codelineno-5-73)| `MODEL_NAME` | `intfloat/multilingual-e5-large` | Embedding model to use (supports multiple models) | [](#__codelineno-5-74)| `PORT` | `31090` | Server port | [](#__codelineno-5-75)| `GPU_COUNT` | `1` | Number of GPUs to use | [](#__codelineno-5-76)| `MAX_EMBED_LEN` | `3072000` | Maximum embedding input length (supports very long documents) | [](#__codelineno-5-77)| `POOLING_TYPE` | `auto` | Model's native pooling type: `auto`, `MEAN`, `CLS`, `LAST` (only affects within-chunk pooling, not cross-chunk aggregation) | [](#__codelineno-5-78)| `API_KEY` | `EMPTY` | API key for authentication | [](#__codelineno-5-79)[](#__codelineno-5-80)## 🔧 How It Works [](#__codelineno-5-81)[](#__codelineno-5-82)1. **Enhanced Input Validation**: `max_embed_len` allows accepting inputs longer than `max_model_len` without environment variables [](#__codelineno-5-83)2. **Smart Chunking**: Text is split based on `max_position_embeddings` to maintain semantic integrity [](#__codelineno-5-84)3. **Unified Processing**: All chunks processed separately through the model using its configured pooling strategy [](#__codelineno-5-85)4. **MEAN Aggregation**: When input exceeds model's native length, results combined using token count-based weighted averaging across all chunks [](#__codelineno-5-86)5. **Consistent Output**: Final embeddings maintain the same dimensionality as standard processing [](#__codelineno-5-87)[](#__codelineno-5-88)### Input Length Handling [](#__codelineno-5-89)[](#__codelineno-5-90)- **Within max_embed_len**: Input is accepted and processed (up to 3M+ tokens) [](#__codelineno-5-91)- **Exceeds max_position_embeddings**: Chunked processing is automatically triggered [](#__codelineno-5-92)- **Exceeds max_embed_len**: Input is rejected with clear error message [](#__codelineno-5-93)- **No environment variables required**: Works without `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN` [](#__codelineno-5-94)[](#__codelineno-5-95)### Extreme Long Text Support [](#__codelineno-5-96)[](#__codelineno-5-97)With `MAX_EMBED_LEN=3072000`, you can process: [](#__codelineno-5-98)[](#__codelineno-5-99)- **Academic papers**: Full research papers with references [](#__codelineno-5-100)- **Legal documents**: Complete contracts and legal texts   [](#__codelineno-5-101)- **Books**: Entire chapters or small books [](#__codelineno-5-102)- **Code repositories**: Large codebases and documentation [](#__codelineno-5-103)[](#__codelineno-5-104)## 📊 Performance Characteristics [](#__codelineno-5-105)[](#__codelineno-5-106)### Chunked Processing Performance [](#__codelineno-5-107)[](#__codelineno-5-108)| Aspect | Behavior | Performance | [](#__codelineno-5-109)| ------ | -------- | ----------- | [](#__codelineno-5-110)| **Chunk Processing** | All chunks processed with native pooling | Consistent with input length | [](#__codelineno-5-111)| **Cross-chunk Aggregation** | MEAN weighted averaging | Minimal overhead | [](#__codelineno-5-112)| **Memory Usage** | Proportional to number of chunks | Moderate, scalable | [](#__codelineno-5-113)| **Semantic Quality** | Complete text coverage | Optimal for long documents | [](#__codelineno-5-114)[](#__codelineno-5-115)## 🧪 Test Cases [](#__codelineno-5-116)[](#__codelineno-5-117)The test client demonstrates: [](#__codelineno-5-118)[](#__codelineno-5-119)- ✅ **Short text**: Normal processing (baseline) [](#__codelineno-5-120)- ✅ **Medium text**: Single chunk processing [](#__codelineno-5-121)- ✅ **Long text**: Multi-chunk processing with aggregation [](#__codelineno-5-122)- ✅ **Very long text**: Many chunks processing [](#__codelineno-5-123)- ✅ **Extreme long text**: Document-level processing (100K+ tokens) [](#__codelineno-5-124)- ✅ **Batch processing**: Mixed-length inputs in one request [](#__codelineno-5-125)- ✅ **Consistency**: Reproducible results across runs [](#__codelineno-5-126)[](#__codelineno-5-127)## 🐛 Troubleshooting [](#__codelineno-5-128)[](#__codelineno-5-129)### Common Issues [](#__codelineno-5-130)[](#__codelineno-5-131)1. **Chunked processing not enabled**: [](#__codelineno-5-132)   [](#__codelineno-5-133)   ```log   [](#__codelineno-5-134)   ValueError: This model's maximum position embeddings length is 4096 tokens...   [](#__codelineno-5-135)   ``` [](#__codelineno-5-136)   [](#__codelineno-5-137)   **Solution**: Ensure `enable_chunked_processing: true` in pooler config [](#__codelineno-5-138)[](#__codelineno-5-139)2. **Input exceeds max_embed_len**: [](#__codelineno-5-140)   [](#__codelineno-5-141)   ```log   [](#__codelineno-5-142)   ValueError: This model's maximum embedding input length is 3072000 tokens...   [](#__codelineno-5-143)   ``` [](#__codelineno-5-144)   [](#__codelineno-5-145)   **Solution**: Increase `max_embed_len` in pooler config or reduce input length [](#__codelineno-5-146)[](#__codelineno-5-147)3. **Memory errors**: [](#__codelineno-5-148)   [](#__codelineno-5-149)   ```log   [](#__codelineno-5-150)   RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory   [](#__codelineno-5-151)   ``` [](#__codelineno-5-152)   [](#__codelineno-5-153)   **Solution**: Reduce chunk size by adjusting model's `max_position_embeddings` or use fewer GPUs [](#__codelineno-5-154)[](#__codelineno-5-155)4. **Slow processing**:    [](#__codelineno-5-156)   **Expected**: Long text takes more time due to multiple inference calls [](#__codelineno-5-157)[](#__codelineno-5-158)### Debug Information [](#__codelineno-5-159)[](#__codelineno-5-160)Server logs show chunked processing activity: [](#__codelineno-5-161)[](#__codelineno-5-162)```log [](#__codelineno-5-163)INFO: Input length 150000 exceeds max_position_embeddings 4096, will use chunked processing [](#__codelineno-5-164)INFO: Split input of 150000 tokens into 37 chunks (max_chunk_size: 4096) [](#__codelineno-5-165)``` [](#__codelineno-5-166)[](#__codelineno-5-167)## 🤝 Contributing [](#__codelineno-5-168)[](#__codelineno-5-169)To extend chunked processing support to other embedding models: [](#__codelineno-5-170)[](#__codelineno-5-171)1. Check model compatibility with the pooling architecture [](#__codelineno-5-172)2. Test with various text lengths [](#__codelineno-5-173)3. Validate embedding quality compared to single-chunk processing [](#__codelineno-5-174)4. Submit PR with test cases and documentation updates [](#__codelineno-5-175)[](#__codelineno-5-176)## 🆕 Enhanced Features [](#__codelineno-5-177)[](#__codelineno-5-178)### max_embed_len Parameter [](#__codelineno-5-179)[](#__codelineno-5-180)The new `max_embed_len` parameter provides: [](#__codelineno-5-181)[](#__codelineno-5-182)- **Simplified Configuration**: No need for `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN` environment variable [](#__codelineno-5-183)- **Flexible Input Validation**: Accept inputs longer than `max_model_len` up to `max_embed_len` [](#__codelineno-5-184)- **Extreme Length Support**: Process documents with millions of tokens [](#__codelineno-5-185)- **Clear Error Messages**: Better feedback when inputs exceed limits [](#__codelineno-5-186)- **Backward Compatibility**: Existing configurations continue to work``

## OpenAI Embedding Long Text - Client[¶](#openai-embedding-long-text-client "Permanent link")

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-6-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-6-3)[](#__codelineno-6-4)""" [](#__codelineno-6-5)Example script demonstrating long text embedding with chunked processing in vLLM. [](#__codelineno-6-6)[](#__codelineno-6-7)This example shows how to use vLLM's chunked processing feature to handle text [](#__codelineno-6-8)inputs that exceed the model's maximum token length. ## Cohere Rerank Client[¶](#cohere-rerank-client "Permanent link")

``[](#__codelineno-0-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-0-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-0-3)""" [](#__codelineno-0-4)Example of using the OpenAI entrypoint's rerank API which is compatible with [](#__codelineno-0-5)the Cohere SDK: https://github.com/cohere-ai/cohere-python [](#__codelineno-0-6)Note that `pip install cohere` is needed to run this example. [](#__codelineno-0-7)[](#__codelineno-0-8)run: vllm serve BAAI/bge-reranker-base [](#__codelineno-0-9)""" [](#__codelineno-0-10)[](#__codelineno-0-11)import cohere [](#__codelineno-0-12)from cohere import Client, ClientV2 [](#__codelineno-0-13)[](#__codelineno-0-14)model = "BAAI/bge-reranker-base" [](#__codelineno-0-15)[](#__codelineno-0-16)query = "What is the capital of France?" [](#__codelineno-0-17)[](#__codelineno-0-18)documents = [     [](#__codelineno-0-19)    "The capital of France is Paris",    [](#__codelineno-0-20)    "Reranking is fun!",    [](#__codelineno-0-21)    "vLLM is an open-source framework for fast AI serving", [](#__codelineno-0-22)] [](#__codelineno-0-23) [](#__codelineno-0-24)[](#__codelineno-0-25)def cohere_rerank(     [](#__codelineno-0-26)    client: Client | ClientV2, model: str, query: str, documents: list[str] [](#__codelineno-0-27)) -> dict:     [](#__codelineno-0-28)    return client.rerank(model=model, query=query, documents=documents) [](#__codelineno-0-29) [](#__codelineno-0-30)[](#__codelineno-0-31)def main():     [](#__codelineno-0-32)    # cohere v1 client    [](#__codelineno-0-33)    cohere_v1 = cohere.Client(base_url="http://localhost:8000", api_key="sk-fake-key")    [](#__codelineno-0-34)    rerank_v1_result = cohere_rerank(cohere_v1, model, query, documents)    [](#__codelineno-0-35)    print("-" * 50)    [](#__codelineno-0-36)    print("rerank_v1_result:\n", rerank_v1_result)    [](#__codelineno-0-37)    print("-" * 50) [](#__codelineno-0-38)    [](#__codelineno-0-39)    # or the v2    [](#__codelineno-0-40)    cohere_v2 = cohere.ClientV2("sk-fake-key", base_url="http://localhost:8000")    [](#__codelineno-0-41)    rerank_v2_result = cohere_rerank(cohere_v2, model, query, documents)    [](#__codelineno-0-42)    print("rerank_v2_result:\n", rerank_v2_result)    [](#__codelineno-0-43)    print("-" * 50) [](#__codelineno-0-44) [](#__codelineno-0-45)[](#__codelineno-0-46)if __name__ == "__main__":     [](#__codelineno-0-47)    main()``

## Colbert Rerank Online[¶](#colbert-rerank-online "Permanent link")

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-1-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-1-3)""" [](#__codelineno-1-4)Example of using ColBERT late interaction models for reranking and scoring. [](#__codelineno-1-5)[](#__codelineno-1-6)ColBERT (Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT) uses per-token embeddings [](#__codelineno-1-7)and MaxSim scoring for document reranking, providing better accuracy than [](#__codelineno-1-8)single-vector models while being more efficient than cross-encoders. [](#__codelineno-1-9)[](#__codelineno-1-10)vLLM supports ColBERT with multiple encoder backbones. Start the server [](#__codelineno-1-11)with one of the following: [](#__codelineno-1-12)    [](#__codelineno-1-13)    # BERT backbone (works out of the box)    [](#__codelineno-1-14)    vllm serve answerdotai/answerai-colbert-small-v1 [](#__codelineno-1-15)    [](#__codelineno-1-16)    # ModernBERT backbone    [](#__codelineno-1-17)    vllm serve lightonai/GTE-ModernColBERT-v1 \        [](#__codelineno-1-18)        --hf-overrides '{"architectures": ["ColBERTModernBertModel"]}' [](#__codelineno-1-19)    [](#__codelineno-1-20)    # Jina XLM-RoBERTa backbone    [](#__codelineno-1-21)    vllm serve jinaai/jina-colbert-v2 \        [](#__codelineno-1-22)        --hf-overrides '{"architectures": ["ColBERTJinaRobertaModel"]}' \        [](#__codelineno-1-23)        --trust-remote-code [](#__codelineno-1-24)[](#__codelineno-1-25)Then run this script:     [](#__codelineno-1-26)    python colbert_rerank_online.py [](#__codelineno-1-27)""" [](#__codelineno-1-28)[](#__codelineno-1-29)import json [](#__codelineno-1-30)[](#__codelineno-1-31)import requests [](#__codelineno-1-32)[](#__codelineno-1-33)# Change this to match the model you started the server with [](#__codelineno-1-34)MODEL = "answerdotai/answerai-colbert-small-v1" [](#__codelineno-1-35)BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000" [](#__codelineno-1-36)[](#__codelineno-1-37)headers = {"accept": "application/json", "Content-Type": "application/json"} [](#__codelineno-1-38)[](#__codelineno-1-39)documents = [     [](#__codelineno-1-40)    "Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence.",    [](#__codelineno-1-41)    "Python is a programming language.",    [](#__codelineno-1-42)    "Deep learning uses neural networks for complex tasks.",    [](#__codelineno-1-43)    "The weather today is sunny.", [](#__codelineno-1-44)] [](#__codelineno-1-45) [](#__codelineno-1-46)[](#__codelineno-1-47)def rerank_example():     [](#__codelineno-1-48)    """Use the /rerank endpoint to rank documents by query relevance."""    [](#__codelineno-1-49)    print("=== Rerank Example ===") [](#__codelineno-1-50)    [](#__codelineno-1-51)    data = {        [](#__codelineno-1-52)        "model": MODEL,        [](#__codelineno-1-53)        "query": "What is machine learning?",        [](#__codelineno-1-54)        "documents": documents,    [](#__codelineno-1-55)    } [](#__codelineno-1-56)    [](#__codelineno-1-57)    response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/rerank", headers=headers, json=data)    [](#__codelineno-1-58)    result = response.json()    [](#__codelineno-1-59)    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2)) [](#__codelineno-1-60)    [](#__codelineno-1-61)    print("\nRanked documents (most relevant first):")    [](#__codelineno-1-62)    for item in result["results"]:        [](#__codelineno-1-63)        doc_idx = item["index"]        [](#__codelineno-1-64)        score = item["relevance_score"]        [](#__codelineno-1-65)        print(f"  Score {score:.4f}: {documents[doc_idx]}") [](#__codelineno-1-66) [](#__codelineno-1-67)[](#__codelineno-1-68)def score_example():     [](#__codelineno-1-69)    """Use the /score endpoint for pairwise query-document scoring."""    [](#__codelineno-1-70)    print("\n=== Score Example ===") [](#__codelineno-1-71)    [](#__codelineno-1-72)    data = {        [](#__codelineno-1-73)        "model": MODEL,        [](#__codelineno-1-74)        "text_1": "What is machine learning?",        [](#__codelineno-1-75)        "text_2": [            [](#__codelineno-1-76)            "Machine learning is a subset of AI.",            [](#__codelineno-1-77)            "The weather is sunny.",        [](#__codelineno-1-78)        ],    [](#__codelineno-1-79)    } [](#__codelineno-1-80)    [](#__codelineno-1-81)    response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/score", headers=headers, json=data)    [](#__codelineno-1-82)    result = response.json()    [](#__codelineno-1-83)    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2)) [](#__codelineno-1-84) [](#__codelineno-1-85)[](#__codelineno-1-86)def main():     [](#__codelineno-1-87)    rerank_example()    [](#__codelineno-1-88)    score_example() [](#__codelineno-1-89) [](#__codelineno-1-90)[](#__codelineno-1-91)if __name__ == "__main__":     [](#__codelineno-1-92)    main()`

## Convert Model To Seq Cls[¶](#convert-model-to-seq-cls "Permanent link")

``[](#__codelineno-5-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-5-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-5-3)# ruff: noqa: E501 [](#__codelineno-5-4)[](#__codelineno-5-5)""" [](#__codelineno-5-6)Script to convert Large Language Models (LLMs) to Sequence Classification models. [](#__codelineno-5-7)This is particularly useful for converting reranker models that use next-token [](#__codelineno-5-8)prediction to a sequence classification format for compatibility with standard [](#__codelineno-5-9)classification and rerank pipelines. [](#__codelineno-5-10)[](#__codelineno-5-11)Usage examples: [](#__codelineno-5-12)- For BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-gemma:   [](#__codelineno-5-13)  python convert_model_to_seq_cls.py --model_name BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-gemma \    [](#__codelineno-5-14)    --classifier_from_tokens '["Yes"]' --method no_post_processing \    [](#__codelineno-5-15)    --path ./bge-reranker-v2-gemma-seq-cls [](#__codelineno-5-16)[](#__codelineno-5-17)- For mxbai-rerank-v2:   [](#__codelineno-5-18)  python convert_model_to_seq_cls.py --model_name mixedbread-ai/mxbai-rerank-base-v2 \    [](#__codelineno-5-19)    --classifier_from_tokens '["0", "1"]' --method from_2_way_softmax \    [](#__codelineno-5-20)    --path ./mxbai-rerank-base-v2-seq-cls [](#__codelineno-5-21)[](#__codelineno-5-22)- For Qwen3-Reranker:   [](#__codelineno-5-23)  python convert_model_to_seq_cls.py --model_name Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B \    [](#__codelineno-5-24)    --classifier_from_tokens '["no", "yes"]' --method from_2_way_softmax \    [](#__codelineno-5-25)    --path ./Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-seq-cls [](#__codelineno-5-26)[](#__codelineno-5-27)Note: For BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-gemma, "Yes" and "yes" are different tokens. ## Forced Alignment Offline[¶](#forced-alignment-offline "Permanent link")

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 [](#__codelineno-0-2)# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project [](#__codelineno-0-3)# Adapted from Qwen3-ForcedAligner inference: [](#__codelineno-0-4)# https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR [](#__codelineno-0-5)[](#__codelineno-0-6)""" [](#__codelineno-0-7)Offline forced alignment example using Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B. [](#__codelineno-0-8)[](#__codelineno-0-9)Forced alignment takes audio and reference text as input and produces [](#__codelineno-0-10)word-level timestamps. The model predicts a time bin at each <timestamp> [](#__codelineno-0-11)token position; multiplying by ``timestamp_segment_time`` gives milliseconds. [](#__codelineno-0-12)[](#__codelineno-0-13)Usage:: [](#__codelineno-0-14)    [](#__codelineno-0-15)    python forced_alignment_offline.py \        [](#__codelineno-0-16)        --model Qwen/Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B [](#__codelineno-0-17)""" [](#__codelineno-0-18)[](#__codelineno-0-19)from argparse import Namespace [](#__codelineno-0-20)[](#__codelineno-0-21)import numpy as np [](#__codelineno-0-22)[](#__codelineno-0-23)from vllm import LLM, EngineArgs [](#__codelineno-0-24)from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser [](#__codelineno-0-25) [](#__codelineno-0-26)[](#__codelineno-0-27)def parse_args():     [](#__codelineno-0-28)    parser = FlexibleArgumentParser()    [](#__codelineno-0-29)    parser = EngineArgs.add_cli_args(parser)    [](#__codelineno-0-30)    parser.set_defaults(        [](#__codelineno-0-31)        model="Qwen/Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B",        [](#__codelineno-0-32)        runner="pooling",        [](#__codelineno-0-33)        enforce_eager=True,        [](#__codelineno-0-34)        hf_overrides={"architectures": ["Qwen3ASRForcedAlignerForTokenClassification"]},    [](#__codelineno-0-35)    )    [](#__codelineno-0-36)    return parser.parse_args() [](#__codelineno-0-37) [](#__codelineno-0-38)[](#__codelineno-0-39)def build_prompt(words: list[str]) -> str:     [](#__codelineno-0-40)    """Build the forced alignment prompt from a word list. [](#__codelineno-0-41)    [](#__codelineno-0-42)    Format: <|audio_start|><|audio_pad|><|audio_end|>            [](#__codelineno-0-43)            word1<timestamp><timestamp>word2<timestamp><timestamp>...    [](#__codelineno-0-44)    """    [](#__codelineno-0-45)    body = "<timestamp><timestamp>".join(words) + "<timestamp><timestamp>"    [](#__codelineno-0-46)    return f"<|audio_start|><|audio_pad|><|audio_end|>{body}" [](#__codelineno-0-47) [](#__codelineno-0-48)[](#__codelineno-0-49)def main(args: Namespace):     [](#__codelineno-0-50)    llm = LLM(**vars(args)) [](#__codelineno-0-51)    [](#__codelineno-0-52)    config = llm.llm_engine.vllm_config.model_config.hf_config    [](#__codelineno-0-53)    timestamp_token_id = config.timestamp_token_id    [](#__codelineno-0-54)    timestamp_segment_time = config.timestamp_segment_time [](#__codelineno-0-55)    [](#__codelineno-0-56)    # Example: align these words against a 5-second audio clip    [](#__codelineno-0-57)    words = ["Hello", "world"]    [](#__codelineno-0-58)    prompt = build_prompt(words) [](#__codelineno-0-59)    [](#__codelineno-0-60)    # Use a 5-second silent audio as placeholder (replace with real audio)    [](#__codelineno-0-61)    sample_rate = 16000    [](#__codelineno-0-62)    audio = np.zeros(sample_rate * 5, dtype=np.float32) [](#__codelineno-0-63)    [](#__codelineno-0-64)    outputs = llm.encode(        [](#__codelineno-0-65)        [{"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"audio": audio}}],        [](#__codelineno-0-66)        pooling_task="token_classify",    [](#__codelineno-0-67)    ) [](#__codelineno-0-68)    [](#__codelineno-0-69)    for output in outputs:        [](#__codelineno-0-70)        logits = output.outputs.data  # [num_tokens, classify_num]        [](#__codelineno-0-71)        predictions = logits.argmax(dim=-1)        [](#__codelineno-0-72)        token_ids = output.prompt_token_ids [](#__codelineno-0-73)        [](#__codelineno-0-74)        # Extract timestamps at <timestamp> positions        [](#__codelineno-0-75)        ts_predictions = [            [](#__codelineno-0-76)            pred.item() * timestamp_segment_time            [](#__codelineno-0-77)            for tid, pred in zip(token_ids, predictions)            [](#__codelineno-0-78)            if tid == timestamp_token_id        [](#__codelineno-0-79)        ] [](#__codelineno-0-80)        [](#__codelineno-0-81)        # Pair up start/end times per word        [](#__codelineno-0-82)        for i, word in enumerate(words):            [](#__codelineno-0-83)            start_ms = ts_predictions[i * 2]            [](#__codelineno-0-84)            end_ms = ts_predictions[i * 2 + 1]            [](#__codelineno-0-85)            print(f"{word:15s} {start_ms / 1000:.3f}s - {end_ms / 1000:.3f}s") [](#__codelineno-0-86) [](#__codelineno-0-87)[](#__codelineno-0-88)if __name__ == "__main__":     [](#__codelineno-0-89)    args = parse_args()    [](#__codelineno-0-90)    main(args)`

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)#!/bin/bash [](#__codelineno-0-2)# [](#__codelineno-0-3)# Helper script to manually start or join a Ray cluster for online serving of vLLM models. [](#__codelineno-0-4)# This script is first executed on the head node, and then on each worker node with the IP address [](#__codelineno-0-5)# of the head node. [](#__codelineno-0-6)# [](#__codelineno-0-7)# Subcommands: [](#__codelineno-0-8)#   leader: Launches a Ray head node and blocks until the cluster reaches the expected size (head + workers). [](#__codelineno-0-9)#   worker: Starts a worker node that connects to an existing Ray head node. [](#__codelineno-0-10)# [](#__codelineno-0-11)# Example usage: [](#__codelineno-0-12)# On the head node machine, start the Ray head node process and run a vLLM server. [](#__codelineno-0-13)#   ./multi-node-serving.sh leader --ray_port=6379 --ray_cluster_size=<SIZE> [<extra ray args>]  && \ [](#__codelineno-0-14)#   vllm serve meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct --port 8080 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline_parallel_size 2 [](#__codelineno-0-15)#  [](#__codelineno-0-16)# On each worker node, start the Ray worker node process.
