# page

[](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/edit/main/docs/features/lora.md "Edit this page")

This document shows you how to use [LoRA adapters](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) with vLLM on top of a base model.

LoRA adapters can be used with any vLLM model that implements [SupportsLoRA](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/api/vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces/#vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces.SupportsLoRA "            SupportsLoRA").

Adapters can be efficiently served on a per-request basis with minimal overhead. First we download the adapter(s) and save them locally with

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download [](#__codelineno-0-2)[](#__codelineno-0-3)sql_lora_path = snapshot_download(repo_id="jeeejeee/llama32-3b-text2sql-spider")`

Then we instantiate the base model and pass in the `enable_lora=True` flag:

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams [](#__codelineno-1-2)from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest [](#__codelineno-1-3)[](#__codelineno-1-4)llm = LLM(model="meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct", enable_lora=True)`

We can now submit the prompts and call `llm.generate` with the `lora_request` parameter. The first parameter of [`LoRARequest`](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/api/vllm/lora/request/#vllm.lora.request.LoRARequest "            LoRARequest") is a human identifiable name, the second parameter is a globally unique ID for the adapter and the third parameter is the path to the LoRA adapter.

Code

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)sampling_params = SamplingParams(     [](#__codelineno-2-2)    temperature=0,    [](#__codelineno-2-3)    max_tokens=256,    [](#__codelineno-2-4)    stop=["[/assistant]"], [](#__codelineno-2-5)) [](#__codelineno-2-6)[](#__codelineno-2-7)prompts = [     [](#__codelineno-2-8)    "[user] Write a SQL query to answer the question based on the table schema.\n\n context: CREATE TABLE table_name_74 (icao VARCHAR, airport VARCHAR)\n\n question: Name the ICAO for lilongwe international airport [/user] [assistant]",    [](#__codelineno-2-9)    "[user] Write a SQL query to answer the question based on the table schema.\n\n context: CREATE TABLE table_name_11 (nationality VARCHAR, elector VARCHAR)\n\n question: When Anchero Pantaleone was the elector what is under nationality? [/user] [assistant]", [](#__codelineno-2-10)] [](#__codelineno-2-11)[](#__codelineno-2-12)outputs = llm.generate(     [](#__codelineno-2-13)    prompts,    [](#__codelineno-2-14)    sampling_params,    [](#__codelineno-2-15)    lora_request=LoRARequest("sql_adapter", 1, sql_lora_path), [](#__codelineno-2-16))`

Check out [examples/features/lora/multilora\_offline.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/features/lora/multilora_offline.py) for an example of how to use LoRA adapters with the async engine and how to use more advanced configuration options.

## Serving LoRA Adapters[¶](#serving-lora-adapters "Permanent link")

LoRA adapted models can also be served with the Open-AI compatible vLLM server. To do so, we use `--lora-modules {name}={path} {name}={path}` to specify each LoRA module when we kick off the server:

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct \     [](#__codelineno-3-2)    --enable-lora \    [](#__codelineno-3-3)    --lora-modules sql-lora=jeeejeee/llama32-3b-text2sql-spider`

The server entrypoint accepts all other LoRA configuration parameters (`max_loras`, `max_lora_rank`, `max_cpu_loras`, etc.), which will apply to all forthcoming requests. Upon querying the `/models` endpoint, we should see our LoRA along with its base model (if `jq` is not installed, you can follow [this guide](https://jqlang.org/download/) to install it.):

Command

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)curl localhost:8000/v1/models | jq . [](#__codelineno-4-2){     [](#__codelineno-4-3)    "object": "list",    [](#__codelineno-4-4)    "data": [        [](#__codelineno-4-5)        {            [](#__codelineno-4-6)            "id": "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct",            [](#__codelineno-4-7)            "object": "model",            [](#__codelineno-4-8)            ...        [](#__codelineno-4-9)        },        [](#__codelineno-4-10)        {            [](#__codelineno-4-11)            "id": "sql-lora",            [](#__codelineno-4-12)            "object": "model",            [](#__codelineno-4-13)            ...        [](#__codelineno-4-14)        }    [](#__codelineno-4-15)    ] [](#__codelineno-4-16)}`

Requests can specify the LoRA adapter as if it were any other model via the `model` request parameter. The requests will be processed according to the server-wide LoRA configuration (i.e. in parallel with base model requests, and potentially other LoRA adapter requests if they were provided and `max_loras` is set high enough).

The following is an example request

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \     [](#__codelineno-5-2)    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \    [](#__codelineno-5-3)    -d '{        [](#__codelineno-5-4)        "model": "sql-lora",        [](#__codelineno-5-5)        "prompt": "San Francisco is a",        [](#__codelineno-5-6)        "max_tokens": 7,        [](#__codelineno-5-7)        "temperature": 0    [](#__codelineno-5-8)    }' | jq`

## Dynamically serving LoRA Adapters[¶](#dynamically-serving-lora-adapters "Permanent link")

In addition to serving LoRA adapters at server startup, the vLLM server supports dynamically configuring LoRA adapters at runtime through dedicated API endpoints and plugins. This feature can be particularly useful when the flexibility to change models on-the-fly is needed.

Warning

This feature comes with security risks. It should not be used in production unless it is an isolated, fully trusted environment.

To enable dynamic LoRA configuration, ensure that the environment variable `VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING` is set to `True`.

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)export VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING=True`

### Using API Endpoints[¶](#using-api-endpoints "Permanent link")

Loading a LoRA Adapter:

To dynamically load a LoRA adapter, send a POST request to the `/v1/load_lora_adapter` endpoint with the necessary details of the adapter to be loaded. The request payload should include the name and path to the LoRA adapter.

Example request to load a LoRA adapter:

`[](#__codelineno-7-1)curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/load_lora_adapter \ [](#__codelineno-7-2)-H "Content-Type: application/json" \ [](#__codelineno-7-3)-d '{     [](#__codelineno-7-4)    "lora_name": "sql_adapter",    [](#__codelineno-7-5)    "lora_path": "/path/to/sql-lora-adapter" [](#__codelineno-7-6)}'`

Upon a successful request, the API will respond with a `200 OK` status code from `vllm serve`, and `curl` returns the response body: `Success: LoRA adapter 'sql_adapter' added successfully`. If an error occurs, such as if the adapter cannot be found or loaded, an appropriate error message will be returned.

Unloading a LoRA Adapter:

To unload a LoRA adapter that has been previously loaded, send a POST request to the `/v1/unload_lora_adapter` endpoint with the name or ID of the adapter to be unloaded.

Upon a successful request, the API responds with a `200 OK` status code from `vllm serve`, and `curl` returns the response body: `Success: LoRA adapter 'sql_adapter' removed successfully`.

Example request to unload a LoRA adapter:

`[](#__codelineno-8-1)curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/unload_lora_adapter \ [](#__codelineno-8-2)-H "Content-Type: application/json" \ [](#__codelineno-8-3)-d '{     [](#__codelineno-8-4)    "lora_name": "sql_adapter" [](#__codelineno-8-5)}'`

### Using Plugins[¶](#using-plugins "Permanent link")

Alternatively, you can use the LoRAResolver plugin to dynamically load LoRA adapters. LoRAResolver plugins enable you to load LoRA adapters from both local and remote sources such as local file system and S3. On every request, when there's a new model name that hasn't been loaded yet, the LoRAResolver will try to resolve and load the corresponding LoRA adapter.

You can set up multiple LoRAResolver plugins if you want to load LoRA adapters from different sources. For example, you might have one resolver for local files and another for S3 storage. vLLM will load the first LoRA adapter that it finds.

You can either install existing plugins or implement your own. By default, vLLM comes with a [resolver plugin to load LoRA adapters from a local directory, as well as a resolver plugin to load LoRA adapters from repositories on Hugging Face Hub](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/vllm/plugins/lora_resolvers) To enable either of these resolvers, you must `set VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING` to True.

-   To leverage a local directory, set `VLLM_PLUGINS` to include `lora_filesystem_resolver` and set `VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR` to a local directory. When vLLM receives a request using a LoRA adapter `foobar`, it will first look in the local directory for a directory `foobar`, and attempt to load the contents of that directory as a LoRA adapter. If successful, the request will complete as normal and that adapter will then be available for normal use on the server.
-   To leverage repositories on Hugging Face Hub, set `VLLM_PLUGINS` to include `lora_hf_hub_resolver` and set `VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_HF_REPO_LIST` to a comma separated list of repository IDs on Hugging Face Hub. When vLLM receives a request for the LoRA adapter `my/repo/subpath`, it will download the adapter at the `subpath` of `my/repo` if it exists and contains an `adapter_config.json`, then build a request to the cached dir for the adapter, similar to the `lora_filesystem_resolver`. Please note that enabling remote downloads is insecure and not intended for use in production environments.

Alternatively, follow these example steps to implement your own plugin:

1.  Implement the LoRAResolver interface.
    
    Example of a simple S3 LoRAResolver implementation
    
    `[](#__codelineno-9-1)import os [](#__codelineno-9-2)import s3fs [](#__codelineno-9-3)from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest [](#__codelineno-9-4)from vllm.lora.resolver import LoRAResolver [](#__codelineno-9-5)[](#__codelineno-9-6)class S3LoRAResolver(LoRAResolver):     [](#__codelineno-9-7)    def __init__(self):        [](#__codelineno-9-8)        self.s3 = s3fs.S3FileSystem()        [](#__codelineno-9-9)        self.s3_path_format = os.getenv("S3_PATH_TEMPLATE")        [](#__codelineno-9-10)        self.local_path_format = os.getenv("LOCAL_PATH_TEMPLATE") [](#__codelineno-9-11)    [](#__codelineno-9-12)    async def resolve_lora(self, base_model_name, lora_name):        [](#__codelineno-9-13)        s3_path = self.s3_path_format.format(base_model_name=base_model_name, lora_name=lora_name)        [](#__codelineno-9-14)        local_path = self.local_path_format.format(base_model_name=base_model_name, lora_name=lora_name) [](#__codelineno-9-15)        [](#__codelineno-9-16)        # Download the LoRA from S3 to the local path        [](#__codelineno-9-17)        await self.s3._get(            [](#__codelineno-9-18)            s3_path, local_path, recursive=True, maxdepth=1        [](#__codelineno-9-19)        ) [](#__codelineno-9-20)        [](#__codelineno-9-21)        lora_request = LoRARequest(            [](#__codelineno-9-22)            lora_name=lora_name,            [](#__codelineno-9-23)            lora_path=local_path,            [](#__codelineno-9-24)            lora_int_id=abs(hash(lora_name)),        [](#__codelineno-9-25)        )        [](#__codelineno-9-26)        return lora_request`
    
2.  Register [`LoRAResolver`](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/api/vllm/lora/resolver/#vllm.lora.resolver.LoRAResolver "            LoRAResolver") plugin.
    
    `[](#__codelineno-10-1)from vllm.lora.resolver import LoRAResolverRegistry [](#__codelineno-10-2)[](#__codelineno-10-3)s3_resolver = S3LoRAResolver() [](#__codelineno-10-4)LoRAResolverRegistry.register_resolver("s3_resolver", s3_resolver)`
    
    For more details, refer to the [vLLM's Plugins System](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/design/plugin_system/).
    

### In-Place LoRA Reloading[¶](#in-place-lora-reloading "Permanent link")

When dynamically loading LoRA adapters, you may need to replace an existing adapter with updated weights while keeping the same name. The `load_inplace` parameter enables this functionality. This commonly occurs in asynchronous reinforcement learning setups, where adapters are continuously updated and swapped in without interrupting ongoing inference.

When `load_inplace=True`, vLLM will replace the existing adapter with the new one.

Example request to load or replace a LoRA adapter with the same name:

`[](#__codelineno-11-1)curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/load_lora_adapter \ [](#__codelineno-11-2)-H "Content-Type: application/json" \ [](#__codelineno-11-3)-d '{     [](#__codelineno-11-4)    "lora_name": "my-adapter",    [](#__codelineno-11-5)    "lora_path": "/path/to/adapter/v2",    [](#__codelineno-11-6)    "load_inplace": true [](#__codelineno-11-7)}'`

## New format for `--lora-modules`[¶](#new-format-for-lora-modules "Permanent link")

In the previous version, users would provide LoRA modules via the following format, either as a key-value pair or in JSON format. For example:

`[](#__codelineno-12-1)--lora-modules  sql-lora=jeeejeee/llama32-3b-text2sql-spider`

This would only include the `name` and `path` for each LoRA module, but did not provide a way to specify a `base_model_name`. Now, you can specify a base\_model\_name alongside the name and path using JSON format. For example:

`[](#__codelineno-13-1)--lora-modules '{"name": "sql-lora", "path": "jeeejeee/llama32-3b-text2sql-spider", "base_model_name": "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct"}'`

To provide the backward compatibility support, you can still use the old key-value format (name=path), but the `base_model_name` will remain unspecified in that case.

## Mixing 2D and 3D MoE LoRA Adapters[¶](#mixing-2d-and-3d-moe-lora-adapters "Permanent link")

To serve 2D-format(based on `megatron`) and 3D-format (based on `peft`) adapters from the same engine instance, start the server with `--enable-mixed-moe-lora-format` and declare the layout of each adapter explicitly via the `is_3d_lora_weight` field.

Server startup (static modules):

`[](#__codelineno-14-1)vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \     [](#__codelineno-14-2)    --enable-lora \    [](#__codelineno-14-3)    --enable-mixed-moe-lora-format \    [](#__codelineno-14-4)    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \    [](#__codelineno-14-5)    --enable-expert-parallel \    [](#__codelineno-14-6)    --lora-modules \        [](#__codelineno-14-7)        '{"name": "lora-2d", "path": "jeeejeee/qwen36-35ba3b-2d-weights-poken-lora", "is_3d_lora_weight": false}' \        [](#__codelineno-14-8)        '{"name": "lora-3d", "path": "jeeejeee/qwen36-35ba3b-moe-all-linear-poken-lora", "is_3d_lora_weight": true}'`

Dynamic load via `/v1/load_lora_adapter`:

`[](#__codelineno-15-1)curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/load_lora_adapter \ [](#__codelineno-15-2)-H "Content-Type: application/json" \ [](#__codelineno-15-3)-d '{     [](#__codelineno-15-4)    "lora_name": "lora-3d",    [](#__codelineno-15-5)    "lora_path": "/path/to/3d-format-lora",    [](#__codelineno-15-6)    "is_3d_lora_weight": true [](#__codelineno-15-7)}'`

You must know your adapter's layout

Under `--enable-mixed-moe-lora-format`, vLLM trusts whatever `is_3d_lora_weight` the caller declares — it does **not** inspect the checkpoint to verify. A wrong declaration will load weights into the wrong stacked buffers and silently produce garbage outputs, with no error at load time. Confirm the layout before serving:

-   **2D (per-expert, megatron-style)** → set `is_3d_lora_weight: false`. Adapter keys look like `...experts.{idx}.gate_proj.lora_A.weight`, `...experts.{idx}.up_proj.lora_A.weight`, `...experts.{idx}.down_proj.lora_A.weight` — one set per expert.
-   **3D (fused, peft-style)** → set `is_3d_lora_weight: true`. Adapter keys look like `...experts.gate_up_proj.lora_A.weight`, `...experts.down_proj.lora_A.weight` — a single tensor that stacks all experts on the leading dim.

When `--enable-mixed-moe-lora-format` is **not** set, `is_3d_lora_weight` is ignored: vLLM picks the wrapper from the base model's `is_3d_moe_weight` and the adapter is required to match. The field is also ignored for non-MoE models.

## LoRA model lineage in model card[¶](#lora-model-lineage-in-model-card "Permanent link")

The new format of `--lora-modules` is mainly to support the display of parent model information in the model card. Here's an explanation of how your current response supports this:

-   The `parent` field of LoRA model `sql-lora` now links to its base model `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct`. This correctly reflects the hierarchical relationship between the base model and the LoRA adapter.
-   The `root` field points to the artifact location of the lora adapter.

Command output

`[](#__codelineno-16-1)$ curl http://localhost:8000/v1/models [](#__codelineno-16-2)[](#__codelineno-16-3){     [](#__codelineno-16-4)    "object": "list",    [](#__codelineno-16-5)    "data": [        [](#__codelineno-16-6)        {        [](#__codelineno-16-7)        "id": "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct",        [](#__codelineno-16-8)        "object": "model",        [](#__codelineno-16-9)        "created": 1715644056,        [](#__codelineno-16-10)        "owned_by": "vllm",        [](#__codelineno-16-11)        "root": "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct",        [](#__codelineno-16-12)        "parent": null,        [](#__codelineno-16-13)        "permission": [            [](#__codelineno-16-14)            {            [](#__codelineno-16-15)            .....            [](#__codelineno-16-16)            }        [](#__codelineno-16-17)        ]        [](#__codelineno-16-18)        },        [](#__codelineno-16-19)        {        [](#__codelineno-16-20)        "id": "sql-lora",        [](#__codelineno-16-21)        "object": "model",        [](#__codelineno-16-22)        "created": 1715644056,        [](#__codelineno-16-23)        "owned_by": "vllm",        [](#__codelineno-16-24)        "root": "jeeejeee/llama32-3b-text2sql-spider",        [](#__codelineno-16-25)        "parent": "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct",        [](#__codelineno-16-26)        "permission": [            [](#__codelineno-16-27)            {            [](#__codelineno-16-28)            ....            [](#__codelineno-16-29)            }        [](#__codelineno-16-30)        ]        [](#__codelineno-16-31)        }    [](#__codelineno-16-32)    ] [](#__codelineno-16-33)}`

## LoRA Support for Tower and Connector of Multi-Modal Model[¶](#lora-support-for-tower-and-connector-of-multi-modal-model "Permanent link")

Currently, vLLM experimentally supports LoRA for the Tower and Connector components of multi-modal models. To enable this feature, you need to implement the corresponding token helper functions for the tower and connector. For more details on the rationale behind this approach, please refer to [PR 26674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/26674). We welcome contributions to extend LoRA support to additional models' tower and connector. Please refer to [Issue 31479](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31479) to check the current model support status.

## Default LoRA Models For Multimodal Models[¶](#default-lora-models-for-multimodal-models "Permanent link")

Some models, e.g., [Granite Speech](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-8b) and [Phi-4-multimodal-instruct](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Phi-4-multimodal-instruct) multimodal, contain LoRA adapter(s) that are expected to always be applied when a given modality is present. This can be a bit tedious to manage with the above approaches, as it requires the user to send the [`LoRARequest`](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/api/vllm/lora/request/#vllm.lora.request.LoRARequest "            LoRARequest") (offline) or to filter requests between the base model and LoRA model (server) depending on the content of the request's multimodal data.

To this end, we allow registration of default multimodal LoRAs to handle this automatically, where users can map each modality to a LoRA adapter to automatically apply it when the corresponding inputs are present. Note that currently, we only allow one LoRA per prompt; if several modalities are provided, each of which are registered to a given modality, none of them will be applied.

Example usage for offline inference

``[](#__codelineno-17-1)from transformers import AutoTokenizer [](#__codelineno-17-2)from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams [](#__codelineno-17-3)from vllm.assets.audio import AudioAsset [](#__codelineno-17-4)[](#__codelineno-17-5)model_id = "ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-2b" [](#__codelineno-17-6)tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id) [](#__codelineno-17-7)[](#__codelineno-17-8)def get_prompt(question: str, has_audio: bool):     [](#__codelineno-17-9)    """Build the input prompt to send to vLLM."""    [](#__codelineno-17-10)    if has_audio:        [](#__codelineno-17-11)        question = f"<|audio|>{question}"    [](#__codelineno-17-12)    chat = [        [](#__codelineno-17-13)        {"role": "user", "content": question},    [](#__codelineno-17-14)    ]    [](#__codelineno-17-15)    return tokenizer.apply_chat_template(chat, tokenize=False) [](#__codelineno-17-16) [](#__codelineno-17-17)[](#__codelineno-17-18)llm = LLM(     [](#__codelineno-17-19)    model=model_id,    [](#__codelineno-17-20)    enable_lora=True,    [](#__codelineno-17-21)    max_lora_rank=64,    [](#__codelineno-17-22)    max_model_len=2048,    [](#__codelineno-17-23)    limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 1},    [](#__codelineno-17-24)    # Will always pass a [`LoRARequest`][vllm.lora.request.LoRARequest] with the `model_id`    [](#__codelineno-17-25)    # whenever audio is contained in the request data.    [](#__codelineno-17-26)    default_mm_loras = {"audio": model_id},    [](#__codelineno-17-27)    enforce_eager=True, [](#__codelineno-17-28)) [](#__codelineno-17-29)[](#__codelineno-17-30)question = "can you transcribe the speech into a written format?" [](#__codelineno-17-31)prompt_with_audio = get_prompt(     [](#__codelineno-17-32)    question=question,    [](#__codelineno-17-33)    has_audio=True, [](#__codelineno-17-34)) [](#__codelineno-17-35)audio = AudioAsset("mary_had_lamb").audio_and_sample_rate [](#__codelineno-17-36)[](#__codelineno-17-37)inputs = {     [](#__codelineno-17-38)    "prompt": prompt_with_audio,    [](#__codelineno-17-39)    "multi_modal_data": {        [](#__codelineno-17-40)        "audio": audio,    [](#__codelineno-17-41)    } [](#__codelineno-17-42)} [](#__codelineno-17-43) [](#__codelineno-17-44)[](#__codelineno-17-45)outputs = llm.generate(     [](#__codelineno-17-46)    inputs,    [](#__codelineno-17-47)    sampling_params=SamplingParams(        [](#__codelineno-17-48)        temperature=0.2,        [](#__codelineno-17-49)        max_tokens=64,    [](#__codelineno-17-50)    ), [](#__codelineno-17-51))``

You can also pass a json dictionary of `--default-mm-loras` mapping modalities to LoRA model IDs. For example, when starting the server:

`[](#__codelineno-18-1)vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-2b \     [](#__codelineno-18-2)    --max-model-len 2048 \    [](#__codelineno-18-3)    --enable-lora \    [](#__codelineno-18-4)    --default-mm-loras '{"audio":"ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-2b"}' \    [](#__codelineno-18-5)    --max-lora-rank 64`

Note: Default multimodal LoRAs are currently only available for `.generate` and chat completions.

## Using Tips[¶](#using-tips "Permanent link")

### Configuring `max_lora_rank`[¶](#configuring-max_lora_rank "Permanent link")

The `--max-lora-rank` parameter controls the maximum rank allowed for LoRA adapters. This setting affects memory allocation and performance:

-   **Set it to the maximum rank** among all LoRA adapters you plan to use
-   **Avoid setting it too high** - using a value much larger than needed wastes memory and can cause performance issues

For example, if your LoRA adapters have ranks \[16, 32, 64\], use `--max-lora-rank 64` rather than 256

`[](#__codelineno-19-1)# Good: matches actual maximum rank [](#__codelineno-19-2)vllm serve model --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 64 [](#__codelineno-19-3)[](#__codelineno-19-4)# Bad: unnecessarily high, wastes memory [](#__codelineno-19-5)vllm serve model --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 256`

### Restricting LoRA to Specific Modules[¶](#restricting-lora-to-specific-modules "Permanent link")

The `--lora-target-modules` parameter allows you to restrict which model modules have LoRA applied at deployment time. This is useful for performance tuning when you only need LoRA on specific layers:

`[](#__codelineno-20-1)# Apply LoRA only to output projection layers [](#__codelineno-20-2)vllm serve model --enable-lora --lora-target-modules o_proj [](#__codelineno-20-3)[](#__codelineno-20-4)# Apply LoRA to multiple specific modules [](#__codelineno-20-5)vllm serve model --enable-lora --lora-target-modules o_proj qkv_proj down_proj`

When `--lora-target-modules` is not specified, LoRA will be applied to all supported modules in the model. This parameter accepts module suffixes (the last component of the module name), such as `o_proj`, `qkv_proj`, `gate_proj`, etc.

# page

[](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/edit/main/docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md "Edit this page")

This page teaches you how to pass multi-modal inputs to [multi-modal models](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/models/supported_models/#list-of-multimodal-language-models) in vLLM.

Note

We are actively iterating on multi-modal support. See [this RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/4194) for upcoming changes, and [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/new/choose) if you have any feedback or feature requests.

Tip

When serving multi-modal models, consider setting `--allowed-media-domains` to restrict domain that vLLM can access to prevent it from accessing arbitrary endpoints that can potentially be vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks. You can provide a list of domains for this arg. For example: `--allowed-media-domains upload.wikimedia.org github.com www.bogotobogo.com`

Also, consider setting `VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS=0` to prevent HTTP redirects from being followed to bypass domain restrictions.

This restriction is especially important if you run vLLM in a containerized environment where the vLLM pods may have unrestricted access to internal networks.

## Offline Inference[¶](#offline-inference "Permanent link")

To input multi-modal data, follow this schema in [vllm.inputs.PromptType](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/api/vllm/inputs/#vllm.inputs.PromptType "            PromptType = DecoderOnlyPrompt | EncoderDecoderPrompt
module-attribute
"):

-   `prompt`: The prompt should follow the format that is documented on HuggingFace.
-   `multi_modal_data`: This is a dictionary that follows the schema defined in [vllm.inputs.MultiModalDataDict](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/api/vllm/inputs/#vllm.inputs.MultiModalDataDict "            MultiModalDataDict = Mapping[str, ModalityData[Any]]
    module-attribute
    ").

### Image Inputs[¶](#image-inputs "Permanent link")

You can pass a single image to the `'image'` field of the multi-modal dictionary, as shown in the following examples:

Code

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-0-2)[](#__codelineno-0-3)llm = LLM(model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf") [](#__codelineno-0-4)[](#__codelineno-0-5)# Refer to the HuggingFace repo for the correct format to use [](#__codelineno-0-6)prompt = "USER: <image>\nWhat is the content of this image?\nASSISTANT:" [](#__codelineno-0-7)[](#__codelineno-0-8)# Load the image using PIL.Image [](#__codelineno-0-9)image = PIL.Image.open(...) [](#__codelineno-0-10)[](#__codelineno-0-11)# Single prompt inference [](#__codelineno-0-12)outputs = llm.generate({     [](#__codelineno-0-13)    "prompt": prompt,    [](#__codelineno-0-14)    "multi_modal_data": {"image": image}, [](#__codelineno-0-15)}) [](#__codelineno-0-16)[](#__codelineno-0-17)for o in outputs:     [](#__codelineno-0-18)    generated_text = o.outputs[0].text    [](#__codelineno-0-19)    print(generated_text) [](#__codelineno-0-20)[](#__codelineno-0-21)# Batch inference [](#__codelineno-0-22)image_1 = PIL.Image.open(...) [](#__codelineno-0-23)image_2 = PIL.Image.open(...) [](#__codelineno-0-24)outputs = llm.generate(     [](#__codelineno-0-25)    [        [](#__codelineno-0-26)        {            [](#__codelineno-0-27)            "prompt": "USER: <image>\nWhat is the content of this image?\nASSISTANT:",            [](#__codelineno-0-28)            "multi_modal_data": {"image": image_1},        [](#__codelineno-0-29)        },        [](#__codelineno-0-30)        {            [](#__codelineno-0-31)            "prompt": "USER: <image>\nWhat's the color of this image?\nASSISTANT:",            [](#__codelineno-0-32)            "multi_modal_data": {"image": image_2},        [](#__codelineno-0-33)        }    [](#__codelineno-0-34)    ] [](#__codelineno-0-35)) [](#__codelineno-0-36)[](#__codelineno-0-37)for o in outputs:     [](#__codelineno-0-38)    generated_text = o.outputs[0].text    [](#__codelineno-0-39)    print(generated_text)`

Full example: [examples/generate/multimodal/vision\_language\_offline.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py)

To substitute multiple images inside the same text prompt, you can pass in a list of images instead:

Code

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-1-2)[](#__codelineno-1-3)llm = LLM(     [](#__codelineno-1-4)    model="microsoft/Phi-3.5-vision-instruct",    [](#__codelineno-1-5)    trust_remote_code=True,  # Required to load Phi-3.5-vision    [](#__codelineno-1-6)    max_model_len=4096,  # Otherwise, it may not fit in smaller GPUs    [](#__codelineno-1-7)    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 2},  # The maximum number to accept [](#__codelineno-1-8)) [](#__codelineno-1-9)[](#__codelineno-1-10)# Refer to the HuggingFace repo for the correct format to use [](#__codelineno-1-11)prompt = "<|user|>\n<|image_1|>\n<|image_2|>\nWhat is the content of each image?<|end|>\n<|assistant|>\n" [](#__codelineno-1-12)[](#__codelineno-1-13)# Load the images using PIL.Image [](#__codelineno-1-14)image1 = PIL.Image.open(...) [](#__codelineno-1-15)image2 = PIL.Image.open(...) [](#__codelineno-1-16)[](#__codelineno-1-17)outputs = llm.generate({     [](#__codelineno-1-18)    "prompt": prompt,    [](#__codelineno-1-19)    "multi_modal_data": {"image": [image1, image2]}, [](#__codelineno-1-20)}) [](#__codelineno-1-21)[](#__codelineno-1-22)for o in outputs:     [](#__codelineno-1-23)    generated_text = o.outputs[0].text    [](#__codelineno-1-24)    print(generated_text)`

Full example: [examples/generate/multimodal/vision\_language\_multi\_image\_offline.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_multi_image_offline.py)

If using the [LLM.chat](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/models/generative_models/#llmchat) method, you can pass images directly in the message content using various formats: image URLs, PIL Image objects, or pre-computed embeddings:

Code

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-2-2)from vllm.assets.image import ImageAsset [](#__codelineno-2-3)[](#__codelineno-2-4)llm = LLM(model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf") [](#__codelineno-2-5)image_url = "https://picsum.photos/id/32/512/512" [](#__codelineno-2-6)image_pil = ImageAsset('cherry_blossom').pil_image [](#__codelineno-2-7)image_embeds = torch.load(...) [](#__codelineno-2-8)[](#__codelineno-2-9)conversation = [     [](#__codelineno-2-10)    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant"},    [](#__codelineno-2-11)    {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},    [](#__codelineno-2-12)    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hello! How can I assist you today?"},    [](#__codelineno-2-13)    {        [](#__codelineno-2-14)        "role": "user",        [](#__codelineno-2-15)        "content": [            [](#__codelineno-2-16)            {                [](#__codelineno-2-17)                "type": "image_url",                [](#__codelineno-2-18)                "image_url": {"url": image_url},            [](#__codelineno-2-19)            },            [](#__codelineno-2-20)            {                [](#__codelineno-2-21)                "type": "image_pil",                [](#__codelineno-2-22)                "image_pil": image_pil,            [](#__codelineno-2-23)            },            [](#__codelineno-2-24)            {                [](#__codelineno-2-25)                "type": "image_embeds",                [](#__codelineno-2-26)                "image_embeds": image_embeds,            [](#__codelineno-2-27)            },            [](#__codelineno-2-28)            {                [](#__codelineno-2-29)                "type": "text",                [](#__codelineno-2-30)                "text": "What's in these images?",            [](#__codelineno-2-31)            },        [](#__codelineno-2-32)        ],    [](#__codelineno-2-33)    }, [](#__codelineno-2-34)] [](#__codelineno-2-35)[](#__codelineno-2-36)# Perform inference and log output. [](#__codelineno-2-37)outputs = llm.chat(conversation) [](#__codelineno-2-38)[](#__codelineno-2-39)for o in outputs:     [](#__codelineno-2-40)    generated_text = o.outputs[0].text    [](#__codelineno-2-41)    print(generated_text)`

Multi-image input can be extended to perform video captioning. We show this with [Qwen2-VL](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct) as it supports videos:

Code

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-3-2)[](#__codelineno-3-3)# Specify the maximum number of frames per video to be 4. This can be changed. [](#__codelineno-3-4)llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct", limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 4}) [](#__codelineno-3-5)[](#__codelineno-3-6)# Create the request payload. [](#__codelineno-3-7)video_frames = ... # load your video making sure it only has the number of frames specified earlier. [](#__codelineno-3-8)message = {     [](#__codelineno-3-9)    "role": "user",    [](#__codelineno-3-10)    "content": [        [](#__codelineno-3-11)        {            [](#__codelineno-3-12)            "type": "text",            [](#__codelineno-3-13)            "text": "Describe this set of frames. Consider the frames to be a part of the same video.",        [](#__codelineno-3-14)        },    [](#__codelineno-3-15)    ], [](#__codelineno-3-16)} [](#__codelineno-3-17)for i in range(len(video_frames)):     [](#__codelineno-3-18)    base64_image = encode_image(video_frames[i]) # base64 encoding.    [](#__codelineno-3-19)    new_image = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/jpeg;base64,{base64_image}"}}    [](#__codelineno-3-20)    message["content"].append(new_image) [](#__codelineno-3-21)[](#__codelineno-3-22)# Perform inference and log output. [](#__codelineno-3-23)outputs = llm.chat([message]) [](#__codelineno-3-24)[](#__codelineno-3-25)for o in outputs:     [](#__codelineno-3-26)    generated_text = o.outputs[0].text    [](#__codelineno-3-27)    print(generated_text)`

#### Custom RGBA Background Color[¶](#custom-rgba-background-color "Permanent link")

When loading RGBA images (images with transparency), vLLM converts them to RGB format. By default, transparent pixels are replaced with white background. You can customize this background color using the `rgba_background_color` parameter in `media_io_kwargs`.

Code

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-4-2)[](#__codelineno-4-3)# Default white background (no configuration needed) [](#__codelineno-4-4)llm = LLM(model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf") [](#__codelineno-4-5)[](#__codelineno-4-6)# Custom black background for dark theme [](#__codelineno-4-7)llm = LLM(     [](#__codelineno-4-8)    model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf",    [](#__codelineno-4-9)    media_io_kwargs={"image": {"rgba_background_color": [0, 0, 0]}}, [](#__codelineno-4-10)) [](#__codelineno-4-11)[](#__codelineno-4-12)# Custom brand color background (e.g., blue) [](#__codelineno-4-13)llm = LLM(     [](#__codelineno-4-14)    model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf",    [](#__codelineno-4-15)    media_io_kwargs={"image": {"rgba_background_color": [0, 0, 255]}}, [](#__codelineno-4-16))`

Note

-   The `rgba_background_color` accepts RGB values as a list `[R, G, B]` or tuple `(R, G, B)` where each value is 0-255
-   This setting only affects RGBA images with transparency; RGB images are unchanged
-   If not specified, the default white background `(255, 255, 255)` is used for backward compatibility

#### Moondream3 Prompt Recipes[¶](#moondream3-prompt-recipes "Permanent link")

[`Moondream3ForCausalLM`](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/api/vllm/model_executor/models/moondream3/#vllm.model_executor.models.moondream3.Moondream3ForCausalLM "            Moondream3ForCausalLM") supports two task-specific prompt formats:

-   `query`: ask a question about the image.
-   `caption`: generate a caption for the image.

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams [](#__codelineno-5-2)from vllm.assets.image import ImageAsset [](#__codelineno-5-3)[](#__codelineno-5-4)llm = LLM(     [](#__codelineno-5-5)    model="moondream/moondream3-preview",    [](#__codelineno-5-6)    tokenizer="moondream/starmie-v1",    [](#__codelineno-5-7)    trust_remote_code=True,    [](#__codelineno-5-8)    max_model_len=2048,    [](#__codelineno-5-9)    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1}, [](#__codelineno-5-10)) [](#__codelineno-5-11)[](#__codelineno-5-12)image = ImageAsset("stop_sign").pil_image [](#__codelineno-5-13) [](#__codelineno-5-14)[](#__codelineno-5-15)def make_query_prompt(question: str) -> str:     [](#__codelineno-5-16)    return (        [](#__codelineno-5-17)        "<|endoftext|><image><|md_reserved_0|>query<|md_reserved_1|>"        [](#__codelineno-5-18)        f"{question}<|md_reserved_2|>"    [](#__codelineno-5-19)    ) [](#__codelineno-5-20) [](#__codelineno-5-21)[](#__codelineno-5-22)def make_caption_prompt(length: str = "normal") -> str:     [](#__codelineno-5-23)    return (        [](#__codelineno-5-24)        "<|endoftext|><image><|md_reserved_0|>"        [](#__codelineno-5-25)        f"describe<|md_reserved_1|>{length}<|md_reserved_2|>"    [](#__codelineno-5-26)    ) [](#__codelineno-5-27) [](#__codelineno-5-28)[](#__codelineno-5-29)query_out = llm.generate(     [](#__codelineno-5-30)    {        [](#__codelineno-5-31)        "prompt": make_query_prompt("What is shown in this image?"),        [](#__codelineno-5-32)        "multi_modal_data": {"image": image},    [](#__codelineno-5-33)    },    [](#__codelineno-5-34)    SamplingParams(max_tokens=64, temperature=0), [](#__codelineno-5-35))[0].outputs[0].text [](#__codelineno-5-36)[](#__codelineno-5-37)caption_out = llm.generate(     [](#__codelineno-5-38)    {        [](#__codelineno-5-39)        "prompt": make_caption_prompt(),        [](#__codelineno-5-40)        "multi_modal_data": {"image": image},    [](#__codelineno-5-41)    },    [](#__codelineno-5-42)    SamplingParams(max_tokens=100, temperature=0), [](#__codelineno-5-43))[0].outputs[0].text [](#__codelineno-5-44)[](#__codelineno-5-45)print("query:", query_out) [](#__codelineno-5-46)print("caption:", caption_out)`

Note

The native Moondream3 model also has `detect` and `point` skills. Those require custom coordinate decoding and are not exposed by this vLLM implementation.

### Video Inputs[¶](#video-inputs "Permanent link")

You can pass a list of NumPy arrays directly to the `'video'` field of the multi-modal dictionary instead of using multi-image input.

Instead of NumPy arrays, you can also pass `'torch.Tensor'` instances, as shown in this example using Qwen2.5-VL:

Code

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)from transformers import AutoProcessor [](#__codelineno-6-2)from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams [](#__codelineno-6-3)from qwen_vl_utils import process_vision_info [](#__codelineno-6-4)[](#__codelineno-6-5)model_path = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct" [](#__codelineno-6-6)video_path = "https://content.pexels.com/videos/free-videos.mp4" [](#__codelineno-6-7)[](#__codelineno-6-8)llm = LLM(     [](#__codelineno-6-9)    model=model_path,    [](#__codelineno-6-10)    gpu_memory_utilization=0.8,    [](#__codelineno-6-11)    enforce_eager=True,    [](#__codelineno-6-12)    limit_mm_per_prompt={"video": 1}, [](#__codelineno-6-13)) [](#__codelineno-6-14)[](#__codelineno-6-15)sampling_params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1024) [](#__codelineno-6-16)[](#__codelineno-6-17)video_messages = [     [](#__codelineno-6-18)    {        [](#__codelineno-6-19)        "role": "system",        [](#__codelineno-6-20)        "content": "You are a helpful assistant.",    [](#__codelineno-6-21)    },    [](#__codelineno-6-22)    {        [](#__codelineno-6-23)        "role": "user",        [](#__codelineno-6-24)        "content": [            [](#__codelineno-6-25)            {"type": "text", "text": "describe this video."},            [](#__codelineno-6-26)            {                [](#__codelineno-6-27)                "type": "video",                [](#__codelineno-6-28)                "video": video_path,                [](#__codelineno-6-29)                "total_pixels": 20480 * 28 * 28,                [](#__codelineno-6-30)                "min_pixels": 16 * 28 * 28,            [](#__codelineno-6-31)            },        [](#__codelineno-6-32)        ]    [](#__codelineno-6-33)    }, [](#__codelineno-6-34)] [](#__codelineno-6-35)[](#__codelineno-6-36)messages = video_messages [](#__codelineno-6-37)processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_path) [](#__codelineno-6-38)prompt = processor.apply_chat_template(     [](#__codelineno-6-39)    messages,    [](#__codelineno-6-40)    tokenize=False,    [](#__codelineno-6-41)    add_generation_prompt=True, [](#__codelineno-6-42)) [](#__codelineno-6-43)[](#__codelineno-6-44)image_inputs, video_inputs = process_vision_info(messages) [](#__codelineno-6-45)mm_data = {} [](#__codelineno-6-46)if video_inputs is not None:     [](#__codelineno-6-47)    mm_data["video"] = video_inputs [](#__codelineno-6-48)[](#__codelineno-6-49)llm_inputs = {     [](#__codelineno-6-50)    "prompt": prompt,    [](#__codelineno-6-51) outputs:     [](#__codelineno-6-56)    generated_text = o.outputs[0].text    [](#__codelineno-6-57)    print(generated_text)`

Note

'process\_vision\_info' is only applicable to Qwen2.5-VL and similar models.

Full example: [examples/generate/multimodal/vision\_language\_offline.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py)

### Audio Inputs[¶](#audio-inputs "Permanent link")

You can pass a tuple `(array, sampling_rate)` to the `'audio'` field of the multi-modal dictionary.

Full example: [examples/generate/multimodal/audio\_language\_offline.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/generate/multimodal/audio_language_offline.py)

#### Chunking Long Audio for Transcription[¶](#chunking-long-audio-for-transcription "Permanent link")

Speech-to-text models like Whisper have a maximum audio length they can process (typically 30 seconds). For longer audio files, vLLM provides a utility to intelligently split audio into chunks at quiet points to minimize cutting through speech.

`[](#__codelineno-7-1)from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams [](#__codelineno-7-2)from vllm.multimodal.audio import split_audio [](#__codelineno-7-3)from vllm.multimodal.media.audio import load_audio [](#__codelineno-7-4)[](#__codelineno-7-5)# Load long audio file [](#__codelineno-7-6)audio, sr = load_audio("long_audio.wav", sr=16000) [](#__codelineno-7-7)[](#__codelineno-7-8)# Split into chunks at low-energy (quiet) regions [](#__codelineno-7-9)chunks = split_audio(     [](#__codelineno-7-10)    audio_data=audio,    [](#__codelineno-7-11)    sample_rate=sr,    [](#__codelineno-7-12)    max_clip_duration_s=30.0,      # Maximum chunk length in seconds    [](#__codelineno-7-13)    overlap_duration_s=1.0,         # Search window for finding quiet split points    [](#__codelineno-7-14)    min_energy_window_size=1600,    # Window size for energy calculation (~100ms at 16kHz) [](#__codelineno-7-15)) [](#__codelineno-7-16)[](#__codelineno-7-17)# Initialize Whisper model [](#__codelineno-7-18)llm = LLM(model="openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo") [](#__codelineno-7-19)sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=256) [](#__codelineno-7-20)[](#__codelineno-7-21)# Transcribe each chunk [](#__codelineno-7-22)transcriptions = [] [](#__codelineno-7-23)for chunk in chunks:     [](#__codelineno-7-24)    outputs = llm.generate({        [](#__codelineno-7-25)        "prompt": "<|startoftranscript|><|en|><|transcribe|><|notimestamps|>",        [](#__codelineno-7-26)        "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (chunk, sr)},    [](#__codelineno-7-27)    }, sampling_params)    [](#__codelineno-7-28)    transcriptions.append(outputs[0].outputs[0].text) [](#__codelineno-7-29)[](#__codelineno-7-30)# Combine results [](#__codelineno-7-31)full_transcription = " ".join(transcriptions)`

The `split_audio` function:

-   Splits audio at quiet points to avoid cutting through speech
-   Uses RMS energy to find low-amplitude regions within the overlap window
-   Preserves all audio samples (no data loss)
-   Supports any sample rate

#### Automatic Audio Channel Normalization[¶](#automatic-audio-channel-normalization "Permanent link")

vLLM automatically normalizes audio channels for models that require specific audio formats. When loading audio with libraries like `torchaudio`, stereo files return shape `[channels, time]`, but many audio models (particularly Whisper-based models) expect mono audio with shape `[time]`.

**Supported models with automatic mono conversion:**

-   **Whisper** and all Whisper-based models
-   **Qwen2-Audio**
-   **Qwen2.5-Omni** / **Qwen3-Omni** (inherits from Qwen2.5-Omni)
-   **Ultravox**

For these models, vLLM automatically:

1.  Detects if the model requires mono audio via the feature extractor
2.  Converts multi-channel audio to mono using channel averaging
3.  Handles both `(channels, time)` format (torchaudio) and `(time, channels)` format (soundfile)

**Example with stereo audio:**

`[](#__codelineno-8-1)import torchaudio [](#__codelineno-8-2)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-8-3)[](#__codelineno-8-4)# Load stereo audio file - returns (channels, time) shape [](#__codelineno-8-5)audio, sr = torchaudio.load("stereo_audio.wav") [](#__codelineno-8-6)print(f"Original shape: {audio.shape}")  # e.g., torch.Size([2, 16000]) [](#__codelineno-8-7)[](#__codelineno-8-8)# vLLM automatically converts to mono for Whisper-based models [](#__codelineno-8-9)llm = LLM(model="openai/whisper-large-v3") [](#__codelineno-8-10)[](#__codelineno-8-11)outputs = llm.generate({     [](#__codelineno-8-12)    "prompt": "",    [](#__codelineno-8-13)    "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (audio.numpy(), sr)}, [](#__codelineno-8-14)})`

No manual conversion is needed - vLLM handles the channel normalization automatically based on the model's requirements.

### Embedding Inputs[¶](#embedding-inputs "Permanent link")

To input pre-computed embeddings belonging to a data type (i.e. image, video, or audio) directly to the language model, pass a tensor of shape `(..., hidden_size of LM)` to the corresponding field of the multi-modal dictionary. The exact shape depends on the model being used.

You must enable this feature via `enable_mm_embeds=True`.

Warning

The vLLM engine may crash if incorrect shape of embeddings is passed. Only enable this flag for trusted users!

#### Image Embeddings[¶](#image-embeddings "Permanent link")

Code

``[](#__codelineno-9-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-9-2)[](#__codelineno-9-3)# Inference with image embeddings as input [](#__codelineno-9-4)llm = LLM(model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf", enable_mm_embeds=True) [](#__codelineno-9-5)[](#__codelineno-9-6)# Refer to the HuggingFace repo for the correct format to use [](#__codelineno-9-7)prompt = "USER: <image>\nWhat is the content of this image?\nASSISTANT:" [](#__codelineno-9-8)[](#__codelineno-9-9)# For most models, `image_embeds` has shape: (num_images, image_feature_size, hidden_size) [](#__codelineno-9-10)image_embeds = torch.load(...) [](#__codelineno-9-11)[](#__codelineno-9-12)outputs = llm.generate({     [](#__codelineno-9-13)    "prompt": prompt,    [](#__codelineno-9-14)    "multi_modal_data": {"image": image_embeds}, [](#__codelineno-9-15)}) [](#__codelineno-9-16)[](#__codelineno-9-17)for o in outputs:     [](#__codelineno-9-18)    generated_text = o.outputs[0].text    [](#__codelineno-9-19)    print(generated_text) [](#__codelineno-9-20)[](#__codelineno-9-21)# Additional examples for models that require extra fields [](#__codelineno-9-22)llm = LLM(     [](#__codelineno-9-23)    "Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct",    [](#__codelineno-9-24)    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 4},    [](#__codelineno-9-25)    enable_mm_embeds=True, [](#__codelineno-9-26)) [](#__codelineno-9-27)mm_data = {     [](#__codelineno-9-28)    "image": {        [](#__codelineno-9-29)        # Shape: (total_feature_size, hidden_size)        [](#__codelineno-9-30)        # total_feature_size = sum(image_feature_size for image in images)        [](#__codelineno-9-31)        "image_embeds": torch.load(...),        [](#__codelineno-9-32)        # Shape: (num_images, 3)        [](#__codelineno-9-33)        # image_grid_thw is needed to calculate positional encoding.        [](#__codelineno-9-34)        "image_grid_thw": torch.load(...),    [](#__codelineno-9-35)    } [](#__codelineno-9-36)} [](#__codelineno-9-37)[](#__codelineno-9-38)llm = LLM(     [](#__codelineno-9-39)    "openbmb/MiniCPM-V-2_6",    [](#__codelineno-9-40)    trust_remote_code=True,    [](#__codelineno-9-41)    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 4},    [](#__codelineno-9-42)    enable_mm_embeds=True, [](#__codelineno-9-43)) [](#__codelineno-9-44)mm_data = {     [](#__codelineno-9-45)    "image": {        [](#__codelineno-9-46)        # Shape: (num_images, num_slices, hidden_size)        [](#__codelineno-9-47)        # num_slices can differ for each image        [](#__codelineno-9-48)        "image_embeds": [torch.load(...) for image in images],        [](#__codelineno-9-49)        # Shape: (num_images, 2)        [](#__codelineno-9-50)        # image_sizes is needed to calculate details of the sliced image.        [](#__codelineno-9-51)        "image_sizes": [image.size for image in images],    [](#__codelineno-9-52)    } [](#__codelineno-9-53)}``

For Qwen3-VL, the `image_embeds` should contain both the base image embedding and deepstack features.

#### Audio Embedding Inputs[¶](#audio-embedding-inputs "Permanent link")

You can pass pre-computed audio embeddings similar to image embeddings:

Code

`[](#__codelineno-10-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-10-2)import torch [](#__codelineno-10-3)[](#__codelineno-10-4)# Enable audio embeddings support [](#__codelineno-10-5)llm = LLM(model="fixie-ai/ultravox-v0_5-llama-3_2-1b", enable_mm_embeds=True) [](#__codelineno-10-6)[](#__codelineno-10-7)# Refer to the HuggingFace repo for the correct format to use [](#__codelineno-10-8)prompt = "USER: <audio>\nWhat is in this audio?\nASSISTANT:" [](#__codelineno-10-9)[](#__codelineno-10-10)# Load pre-computed audio embeddings, usually with shape: [](#__codelineno-10-11)# (num_audios, audio_feature_size, hidden_size of LM) [](#__codelineno-10-12)audio_embeds = torch.load(...) [](#__codelineno-10-13)[](#__codelineno-10-14)outputs = llm.generate({     [](#__codelineno-10-15)    "prompt": prompt,    [](#__codelineno-10-16)    "multi_modal_data": {"audio": audio_embeds}, [](#__codelineno-10-17)}) [](#__codelineno-10-18)[](#__codelineno-10-19)for o in outputs:     [](#__codelineno-10-20)    generated_text = o.outputs[0].text    [](#__codelineno-10-21)    print(generated_text)`

### Cached Inputs[¶](#cached-inputs "Permanent link")

When using multi-modal inputs, vLLM normally hashes each media item by content to enable caching across requests. You can optionally pass `multi_modal_uuids` to provide your own stable IDs for each item so caching can reuse work across requests without rehashing the raw content.

Code

`[](#__codelineno-11-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-11-2)from PIL import Image [](#__codelineno-11-3)[](#__codelineno-11-4)# Qwen2.5-VL example with two images [](#__codelineno-11-5)llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct") [](#__codelineno-11-6)[](#__codelineno-11-7)prompt = "USER: <image><image>\nDescribe the differences.\nASSISTANT:" [](#__codelineno-11-8)img_a = Image.open("/path/to/a.jpg") [](#__codelineno-11-9)img_b = Image.open("/path/to/b.jpg") [](#__codelineno-11-10)[](#__codelineno-11-11)outputs = llm.generate({     [](#__codelineno-11-12)    "prompt": prompt,    [](#__codelineno-11-13)    "multi_modal_data": {"image": [img_a, img_b]},    [](#__codelineno-11-14)    # Provide stable IDs for caching.    [](#__codelineno-11-15)    # Requirements (matched by this example):    [](#__codelineno-11-16)    #  - Include every modality present in multi_modal_data.    [](#__codelineno-11-17)    #  - For lists, provide the same number of entries.    [](#__codelineno-11-18)    #  - Use None to fall back to content hashing for that item.    [](#__codelineno-11-19)    "multi_modal_uuids": {"image": ["sku-1234-a", None]}, [](#__codelineno-11-20)}) [](#__codelineno-11-21)[](#__codelineno-11-22)for o in outputs:     [](#__codelineno-11-23)    print(o.outputs[0].text)`

Using UUIDs, you can also skip sending media data entirely if you expect cache hits for respective items. Note that the request will fail if the skipped media doesn't have a corresponding UUID, or if the UUID fails to hit the cache.

Code

`[](#__codelineno-12-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-12-2)from PIL import Image [](#__codelineno-12-3)[](#__codelineno-12-4)# Qwen2.5-VL example with two images [](#__codelineno-12-5)llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct") [](#__codelineno-12-6)[](#__codelineno-12-7)prompt = "USER: <image><image>\nDescribe the differences.\nASSISTANT:" [](#__codelineno-12-8)img_b = Image.open("/path/to/b.jpg") [](#__codelineno-12-9)[](#__codelineno-12-10)outputs = llm.generate({     [](#__codelineno-12-11)    "prompt": prompt,    [](#__codelineno-12-12)    "multi_modal_data": {"image": [None, img_b]},    [](#__codelineno-12-13)    # Since img_a is expected to be cached, we can skip sending the actual    [](#__codelineno-12-14)    # image entirely.    [](#__codelineno-12-15)    "multi_modal_uuids": {"image": ["sku-1234-a", None]}, [](#__codelineno-12-16)}) [](#__codelineno-12-17)[](#__codelineno-12-18)for o in outputs:     [](#__codelineno-12-19)    print(o.outputs[0].text)`

Warning

If both multimodal processor caching and prefix caching are disabled, user-provided `multi_modal_uuids` are ignored.

## Online Serving[¶](#online-serving "Permanent link")

Our OpenAI-compatible server accepts multi-modal data via the [Chat Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat). Media inputs also support optional UUIDs users can provide to uniquely identify each media, which is used to cache the media results across requests.

Important

A chat template is **required** to use Chat Completions API. For HF format models, the default chat template is defined inside `chat_template.json` or `tokenizer_config.json`.

If no default chat template is available, we will first look for a built-in fallback in [vllm/transformers\_utils/chat\_templates/registry.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/transformers_utils/chat_templates/registry.py). If no fallback is available, an error is raised and you have to provide the chat template manually via the `--chat-template` argument.

For certain models, we provide alternative chat templates inside [examples](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples). For example, VLM2Vec uses [examples/pooling/embed/template/vlm2vec\_phi3v.jinja](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/pooling/embed/template/vlm2vec_phi3v.jinja) which is different from the default one for Phi-3-Vision.

### Image Inputs[¶](#image-inputs_1 "Permanent link")

Image input is supported according to [OpenAI Vision API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/vision). Here is a simple example using Phi-3.5-Vision.

First, launch the OpenAI-compatible server:

`[](#__codelineno-13-1)vllm serve microsoft/Phi-3.5-vision-instruct --runner generate \   [](#__codelineno-13-2)  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 4096 --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 2`

Then, you can use the OpenAI client as follows:

Code

``[](#__codelineno-14-1)import os [](#__codelineno-14-2)from openai import OpenAI [](#__codelineno-14-3)[](#__codelineno-14-4)openai_api_key = "EMPTY" [](#__codelineno-14-5)openai_api_base = "http://localhost:8000/v1" [](#__codelineno-14-6)[](#__codelineno-14-7)client = OpenAI(     [](#__codelineno-14-8)    api_key=openai_api_key,    [](#__codelineno-14-9)    base_url=openai_api_base, [](#__codelineno-14-10)) [](#__codelineno-14-11)[](#__codelineno-14-12)# Single-image input inference [](#__codelineno-14-13)[](#__codelineno-14-14)# Public image URL for testing remote image processing [](#__codelineno-14-15)image_url = "https://vllm-public-assets.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/vision_model_images/2560px-Gfp-wisconsin-madison-the-nature-boardwalk.jpg" [](#__codelineno-14-16)[](#__codelineno-14-17)# Create chat completion with remote image [](#__codelineno-14-18)chat_response = client.chat.completions.create(     [](#__codelineno-14-19)    model="microsoft/Phi-3.5-vision-instruct",    [](#__codelineno-14-20)    messages=[        [](#__codelineno-14-21)        {            [](#__codelineno-14-22)            "role": "user",            [](#__codelineno-14-23)            "content": [                [](#__codelineno-14-24)                # NOTE: The prompt formatting with the image token `<image>` is not needed                [](#__codelineno-14-25)                # since the prompt will be processed automatically by the API server. Full example: [examples/generate/multimodal/openai\_chat\_completion\_client\_for\_multimodal.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/generate/multimodal/openai_chat_completion_client_for_multimodal.py)

Tip

Loading from local file paths is also supported on vLLM: You can specify the allowed local media path via `--allowed-local-media-path` when launching the API server/engine, and pass the file path as `url` in the API request.

Tip

There is no need to place image placeholders in the text content of the API request - they are already represented by the image content. In fact, you can place image placeholders in the middle of the text by interleaving text and image content.

Note

By default, the timeout for fetching images through HTTP URL is `5` seconds. You can override this by setting the environment variable:

`[](#__codelineno-15-1)export VLLM_IMAGE_FETCH_TIMEOUT=<timeout>`

### Video Inputs[¶](#video-inputs_1 "Permanent link")

Instead of `image_url`, you can pass a video file via `video_url`. Here is a simple example using [LLaVA-OneVision](https://huggingface.co/llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf).

First, launch the OpenAI-compatible server:

`[](#__codelineno-16-1)vllm serve llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf --runner generate --max-model-len 8192`

Then, you can use the OpenAI client as follows:

Code

`[](#__codelineno-17-1)from openai import OpenAI [](#__codelineno-17-2)[](#__codelineno-17-3)openai_api_key = "EMPTY" [](#__codelineno-17-4)openai_api_base = "http://localhost:8000/v1" [](#__codelineno-17-5)[](#__codelineno-17-6)client = OpenAI(     [](#__codelineno-17-7)    api_key=openai_api_key,    [](#__codelineno-17-8)    base_url=openai_api_base, [](#__codelineno-17-9)) [](#__codelineno-17-10)[](#__codelineno-17-11)video_url = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/raushan-testing-hf/videos-test/resolve/main/sample_demo_1.mp4" [](#__codelineno-17-12)[](#__codelineno-17-13)## Use video url in the payload [](#__codelineno-17-14)chat_completion_from_url = client.chat.completions.create(     [](#__codelineno-17-15)    messages=[        [](#__codelineno-17-16)        {            [](#__codelineno-17-17)            "role": "user",            [](#__codelineno-17-18)            "content": [                [](#__codelineno-17-19)                {                    [](#__codelineno-17-20)                    "type": "text",                    [](#__codelineno-17-21)                    "text": "What's in this video?",                [](#__codelineno-17-22)                },                [](#__codelineno-17-23)                {                    [](#__codelineno-17-24)                    "type": "video_url",                    [](#__codelineno-17-25)                    "video_url": {"url": video_url},                    [](#__codelineno-17-26)                    "uuid": video_url,  # Optional                [](#__codelineno-17-27)                },            [](#__codelineno-17-28)            ],        [](#__codelineno-17-29)        }    [](#__codelineno-17-30)    ],    [](#__codelineno-17-31)    model=model,    [](#__codelineno-17-32)    max_completion_tokens=64, [](#__codelineno-17-33)) [](#__codelineno-17-34)[](#__codelineno-17-35)result = chat_completion_from_url.choices[0].message.content [](#__codelineno-17-36)print("Chat completion output from image url:", result)`

Full example: [examples/generate/multimodal/openai\_chat\_completion\_client\_for\_multimodal.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/generate/multimodal/openai_chat_completion_client_for_multimodal.py)

Note

By default, the timeout for fetching videos through HTTP URL is `30` seconds. You can override this by setting the environment variable:

`[](#__codelineno-18-1)export VLLM_VIDEO_FETCH_TIMEOUT=<timeout>`

#### Video Frame Recovery[¶](#video-frame-recovery "Permanent link")

For improved robustness when processing potentially corrupted or truncated video files, vLLM supports optional frame recovery using a dynamic window forward-scan approach. When enabled, if a target frame fails to load during sequential reading, the next successfully grabbed frame (before the next target frame) will be used in its place.

To enable video frame recovery, pass the `frame_recovery` parameter via `--media-io-kwargs`:

`[](#__codelineno-19-1)# Example: Enable frame recovery [](#__codelineno-19-2)vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct \   [](#__codelineno-19-3)  --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"frame_recovery": true}}'`

**Parameters:**

-   `frame_recovery`: Boolean flag to enable forward-scan recovery. When `true`, failed frames are recovered using the next available frame within the dynamic window (up to the next target frame). Default is `false`.

**How it works:**

1.  The system reads frames sequentially
2.  If a target frame fails to grab, it's marked as "failed"
3.  The next successfully grabbed frame (before reaching the next target) is used to recover the failed frame
4.  This approach handles both mid-video corruption and end-of-video truncation

Works with common video formats like MP4 when using OpenCV backends.

When you extract video frames on the client side and send them as `video/jpeg` (base64-concatenated JPEG frames), you can preserve the original video metadata by using `media_io_kwargs` in your request. This enables more accurate video understanding by preserving temporal information that would otherwise be lost during client-side frame extraction.

**Supported Parameters:**

Parameter

Type

Description

`fps`

float

Frame rate of the original video

`frames_indices`

list\[int\]

Indices of the actually sampled frames

`total_num_frames`

int

Total frame count of the original video

`duration`

float

Duration of the original video in seconds

`do_sample_frames`

bool

Whether to perform frame sampling

Code

`[](#__codelineno-20-1)from openai import OpenAI [](#__codelineno-20-2)[](#__codelineno-20-3)client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") [](#__codelineno-20-4)[](#__codelineno-20-5)# Client-side frame extraction [](#__codelineno-20-6)frames = extract_frames(video_path, num_frames=32) [](#__codelineno-20-7)frames_b64 = ",".join([encode_image(f) for f in frames]) [](#__codelineno-20-8)video_url = f"data:video/jpeg;base64,{frames_b64}" [](#__codelineno-20-9)[](#__codelineno-20-10)# Pass video metadata via media_io_kwargs [](#__codelineno-20-11)response = client.chat.completions.create(     [](#__codelineno-20-12)    model="your-multimodal-model",    [](#__codelineno-20-13)    messages=[{        [](#__codelineno-20-14)        "role": "user",        [](#__codelineno-20-15)        "content": [            [](#__codelineno-20-16)            {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": video_url}},            [](#__codelineno-20-17)            {"type": "text", "text": "Describe what happens in this video."}        [](#__codelineno-20-18)        ]    [](#__codelineno-20-19)    }],    [](#__codelineno-20-20)    extra_body={        [](#__codelineno-20-21)        "media_io_kwargs": {            [](#__codelineno-20-22)            "video": {                [](#__codelineno-20-23)                               [](#__codelineno-20-27)                                   260, 270, 280, 290, 300, 310],                [](#__codelineno-20-28)                "total_num_frames": 900,                [](#__codelineno-20-29)                "duration": 30.0,            [](#__codelineno-20-30)            }        [](#__codelineno-20-31)        }    [](#__codelineno-20-32)    }, [](#__codelineno-20-33)) [](#__codelineno-20-34)[](#__codelineno-20-35)print(response.choices[0].message.content)`

**Why use `media_io_kwargs`?**

When extracting frames client-side, the server loses important context about the original video:

-   **Temporal information**: Which frames were sampled and their positions in the original timeline
-   **Video duration**: How long the original video was
-   **Frame rate**: The original playback speed

By passing this metadata, the model can better understand the temporal distribution of the sampled frames and whether important moments might have been skipped.

#### Custom RGBA Background Color[¶](#custom-rgba-background-color_1 "Permanent link")

To use a custom background color for RGBA images, pass the `rgba_background_color` parameter via `--media-io-kwargs`:

`[](#__codelineno-21-1)# Example: Black background for dark theme [](#__codelineno-21-2)vllm serve llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf \   [](#__codelineno-21-3)  --media-io-kwargs '{"image": {"rgba_background_color": [0, 0, 0]}}' [](#__codelineno-21-4)[](#__codelineno-21-5)# Example: Custom gray background [](#__codelineno-21-6)vllm serve llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf \   [](#__codelineno-21-7)  --media-io-kwargs '{"image": {"rgba_background_color": [128, 128, 128]}}'`

`[](#__codelineno-22-1)vllm serve fixie-ai/ultravox-v0_5-llama-3_2-1b`

### Embedding Inputs[¶](#embedding-inputs_1 "Permanent link")

To input pre-computed embeddings belonging to a data type (i.e. image, video, or audio) directly to the language model, pass a tensor of shape `(..., hidden_size of LM)` for each item to the corresponding field of the multi-modal dictionary.

Important

Unlike offline inference, the embeddings for each item must be passed separately in order for placeholder tokens to be applied correctly by the chat template.

You must enable this feature via the `--enable-mm-embeds` flag in `vllm serve`.

Warning

The vLLM engine may crash if incorrect shape of embeddings is passed. Only enable this flag for trusted users!

#### Image Embedding Inputs[¶](#image-embedding-inputs "Permanent link")

For image embeddings, you can pass the base64-encoded tensor to the `image_embeds` field. The following example demonstrates how to pass image embeddings to the OpenAI server:

# page

[](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/edit/main/docs/features/sleep_mode.md "Edit this page")

vLLM's Sleep Mode allows you to temporarily release most GPU memory used by a model, including model weights and KV cache, without stopping the server or unloading the Docker container. This is especially useful for RLHF, training, or cost-saving scenarios where GPU resources need to be freed between inference workloads.

Key benefits:

-   **Frees GPU memory**: Offloads model weights to CPU RAM and discards KV cache, releasing up to 90%+ of GPU memory for other tasks.
-   **Fast resume**: Quickly wake up the engine and resume inference without full model reload.
-   **API endpoints**: Control sleep/wake\_up state via HTTP endpoints or Python API.
-   **Supports distributed workloads**: Works with tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, etc.
-   **Fine-grained control**: Optionally wake up only model weights or KV cache to avoid OOM during weight updates.

Note

This feature is now supported on CUDA and ROCm platform.

Note

For more information, see this [Blog Post](https://blog.vllm.ai/2025/10/26/sleep-mode.html).

## Sleep levels[¶](#sleep-levels "Permanent link")

Level 1 sleep will offload the model weights and discard the KV cache. The content of KV cache is forgotten. Level 1 sleep is good for sleeping and waking up the engine to run the same model again. The model weights are backed up in CPU memory. Please make sure there's enough CPU memory to store the model weights. Level 2 sleep will discard both the model weights and the KV cache (while the model's buffers are kept in CPU, like rope scaling tensors). The content of both the model weights and KV cache is forgotten. Level 2 sleep is good for sleeping and waking up the engine to run a different model or update the model, where previous model weights are not needed, e.g. RLHF weight update.

## Usage[¶](#usage "Permanent link")

### Offline inference[¶](#offline-inference "Permanent link")

Enable sleep mode by passing `enable_sleep_mode=True` to the [`LLM`](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/api/vllm/entrypoints/llm/#vllm.entrypoints.llm.LLM "            LLM") class.

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)from vllm import LLM [](#__codelineno-0-2)llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", enable_sleep_mode=True)`

#### Python API[¶](#python-api "Permanent link")

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)# Sleep level 1 [](#__codelineno-1-2)# Put the engine to sleep (level=1: offload weights to CPU RAM, discard KV cache) [](#__codelineno-1-3)llm.sleep(level=1) [](#__codelineno-1-4)[](#__codelineno-1-5)# Wake up the engine (restore weights) [](#__codelineno-1-6)llm.wake_up()`

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)# Sleep level 2 [](#__codelineno-2-2)# Put the engine to sleep (level=2: discard both weights and KV cache) [](#__codelineno-2-3)llm.sleep(level=2) [](#__codelineno-2-4)[](#__codelineno-2-5)# Reallocate weights memory only [](#__codelineno-2-6)llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"]) [](#__codelineno-2-7)[](#__codelineno-2-8)# Load weights in-place [](#__codelineno-2-9)llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights") [](#__codelineno-2-10)[](#__codelineno-2-11)# Reallocate KV cache [](#__codelineno-2-12)llm.wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])`

#### RLHF weight updates[¶](#rlhf-weight-updates "Permanent link")

During RLHF training, vLLM allows you to selectively wake up only the model weights or the KV cache using the tags argument in wake\_up(). This fine-grained control is especially useful when updating model weights: by waking up just the weights (e.g., llm.wake\_up(tags=\["weights"\])), you avoid allocating memory for the KV cache until after the weight update is complete. This approach helps prevent GPU out-of-memory (OOM) errors, particularly with large models, by minimizing peak memory usage during weight synchronization and update operations.

Use `tags=["weights"]` or `tags=["kv_cache"]` to control which resources are restored, useful for RLHF and weight updates. **Note** that `is_sleeping` will report `true` until all components are awake.

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)# Put engine to deep sleep (level=2) [](#__codelineno-3-2)llm.sleep(level=2) [](#__codelineno-3-3)# ... Get the new weights [](#__codelineno-3-4)# Wake up only weights to avoid OOM [](#__codelineno-3-5)llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"]) [](#__codelineno-3-6)# ... Update the weights [](#__codelineno-3-7)# wake up KV cache after weights are updated [](#__codelineno-3-8)llm.wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])`

### Online Serving[¶](#online-serving "Permanent link")

To enable sleep mode in a vLLM server you need to initialize it with the flag `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` and pass `--enable-sleep-mode` to the vLLM server.

#### Server in development mode[¶](#server-in-development-mode "Permanent link")

When using the flag `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` you enable development endpoints, and these endpoints should not be exposed to users.

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \   [](#__codelineno-4-2)  --enable-sleep-mode \  [](#__codelineno-4-3)  --port 8000`

Below is an example of how to sleep and wake up a model in level 1.

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/sleep?level=1' [](#__codelineno-5-2)curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/wake_up'`

And this is an example of how to sleep and wake up a model in level 2.

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/sleep?level=2' [](#__codelineno-6-2)# Reallocate weights memory only [](#__codelineno-6-3)curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/wake_up?tags=weights' [](#__codelineno-6-4)# Load weights in-place [](#__codelineno-6-5)curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/collective_rpc' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"method":"reload_weights"}' [](#__codelineno-6-6)# Reallocate KV cache [](#__codelineno-6-7)curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/wake_up?tags=kv_cache'`

#### HTTP endpoints[¶](#http-endpoints "Permanent link")

-   `POST /sleep?level=1` — Put the model to sleep (`level=1`).
-   `POST /wake_up` — Wake up the model. Supports optional `tags` query parameters for partial wake-up (e.g., `?tags=weights`).
-   `POST /collective_rpc` — Perform a collective remote procedure call (RPC).
-   `GET /is_sleeping` — Check if the model is sleeping.

Note

These endpoints are only available when passing `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`.

## Limitation[¶](#limitation "Permanent link")

On ROCm, the virtual memory allocation on ROCm is done through chunked memory allocation. You can control the chunk size through `VLLM_ROCM_SLEEP_MEM_CHUNK_SIZE` (in MB). The default value is set at 256MB. The larger the chunk size the faster the performance. However, setting it too large will cause OOM. So if you encounter OOM when using sleep mode. Try reducing the chunk size. It is recommended to define the chunk size as a power of 2.

---

# page

[](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/edit/main/docs/features/reasoning_outputs.md "Edit this page")

vLLM offers support for reasoning models like [DeepSeek R1](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1), which are designed to generate outputs containing both reasoning steps and final conclusions.

Reasoning models return an additional `reasoning` field in their outputs, which contains the reasoning steps that led to the final conclusion. This field is not present in the outputs of other models.

Warning

`reasoning` used to be called `reasoning_content`. To migrate, directly replace `reasoning_content` with `reasoning`.

## Supported Models[¶](#supported-models "Permanent link")

vLLM currently supports the following reasoning models:

❌
